# Session 10 (Opus): make it deployable and safe for real users, before the VPS arrives Wed Nov 18

Follow the session ritual in CLAUDE.md. Read `CLAUDE.md`, then `docs/STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION.md`, then `docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`,
then `deploy/` (every file in it). **Don't read the whole codebase.** Post a plan of 10 lines at most and start without waiting.
Stop and ask only for something that can't be undone, or if a rule below conflicts with the code.

Repo: `c:\Users\Aarushi\Downloads\LaunchWitness`, branch from `main` (at `99fdd11` or later): `s10-production-ready`.
Windows + Git Bash. Tests: `cd backend && ../.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q | tail -5`. Lint: `../.venv/Scripts/python -m ruff check .`.
Frontend: `npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build`. Docker Desktop is installed (`docker` is on PATH). There's no `gh`: merge locally with
`git merge --no-ff` and push.

**Why this session:** LaunchWitness is a real product for real sellers, not just a demo. Phases 1–3 are merged (477 tests), but
**nobody has built the Docker image or run the full stack since the accounts and proof-chain code landed.** The new code
depends on things the old deploy may not do: `__Host-` cookies need real HTTPS, the request guard needs the right Host and
X-Forwarded-For from Caddy, `/internal/tls-ask` must not be reachable from outside, the scheduler must run exactly once, and
there are new env vars. On Wednesday the VPS deploy must be boring. Make it boring now.

---

## Part A: the full stack runs in Docker exactly as it will on the VPS (the most important part)

1. **Audit `deploy/`** (Dockerfile(s), `docker-compose.yml`, Caddyfile, `scripts/check_m1.sh`, `scripts/backup_db.sh`) against
   the current code. Write down every mismatch before fixing anything. At minimum, check:
   - The image builds from a clean clone: the frontend build is baked in, `/build` (the replay) is served, and there's no dev dependency in the runtime image.
   - The app runs as a **non-root** user, with a healthcheck (`/api/health`) and `restart: unless-stopped`.
   - **Exactly one app process** (one uvicorn worker), because APScheduler runs in-process and SQLite has one writer.
     Add a startup guard or comment, so nobody "scales" it to 4 workers and gets 4 copies of every alert and test order.
   - Only Caddy publishes ports (80/443). The app port is **not** published, since `visitor_id` trusts the last X-Forwarded-For entry.
   - Caddy: the app on `launchwitness.com`; shops through **on-demand TLS** with `ask` → `/internal/tls-ask`;
     **`/internal/*` answers 404 from outside on every host**; it passes Host and appends X-Forwarded-For; HSTS on the app host;
     sensible timeouts and body-size limit (photo uploads).
   - **Per-shop A records, no wildcard** (this was decided in S9F). Update RUNBOOK_M1 and the DNS plan wherever they still say
     "wildcard". The app's own `A @` → VPS is the only hand-made record, plus `www` if wanted.
   - The SQLite file sits on a named volume; uploads sit on a volume; `.env` is only on the server, `chmod 600`, never in the image.
2. **Run it locally the production way:** `docker compose` with Caddy using `tls internal` (a local CA) on hostnames like
   `launchwitness.localhost` and `meera.launchwitness.localhost`, with **`DEV_MODE=false`**, `USE_FAKES=true`, `CLAUDE_MODE=fixture`,
   and SMTP pointed at a local catch-all (for example a tiny `aiosmtpd` or MailHog container), so no real email leaves.
   Add this as `deploy/docker-compose.local.yml` (an override) plus `deploy/README.md`. Then prove, with commands and output in the report:
   - `__Host-lw_session` is set with Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax/no Domain, and the browser keeps it over https.
   - sign in → My shops → describe → practice launch → report works through Caddy (Playwright against the https URL,
     accepting the local CA only in this script).
   - A shop host gets 404 for `/api/*` and `/internal/*`. `/internal/tls-ask` from outside → 404. Inside the compose network → works.
   - Rate limits see the real client IP through Caddy (not Caddy's IP, and not a header the client forged).
   - `docker compose restart app` → the startup reconciler runs, nothing is left "running", and the scheduler has exactly one set of jobs.
   - Kill the app mid-launch → the plan shows "Server restarted, press Resume".
3. **`scripts/check_m1.sh`**: update it for the new stack (health, HTTPS on the app, the cookie flags, `/internal` blocked, the shop-host
   guard, the mailbox-expiry warning field, the ADMIN_EMAIL user exists). It must run against both the local stack and the VPS.

## Part B: data safety for real users

- **SQLite done properly:** WAL mode, `busy_timeout` (for example 5 s), `foreign_keys=ON`, set on every connection (an SQLAlchemy
  `connect` event). Test it. Keep SQLite: it's right for one VPS at this scale. Write in SPEC when we'd move to Postgres (more than one
  server, or heavy concurrent writes) and that SQLModel makes that move small.
- **Backups:** `backup_db.sh` must use SQLite's online backup (`.backup` or `VACUUM INTO`, never `cp` of a live WAL database), keep 7
  daily copies plus 4 weekly, and have a **tested restore** (`scripts/restore_db.sh` plus a test that backs up, restores and compares row counts).
  Document a cron line for the VPS. An off-server copy is a manual TODO for the owner (say so plainly; don't invent a cloud service).
- **Migrations:** `add_missing_columns` stays. Add a test that a database file from before S9F (no users/sessions tables, the old
  business columns) starts up cleanly and keeps its rows.
- **Startup self-check** (log, plus `/api/health` → `warnings: [...]`, which never shows secrets): ADMIN_EMAIL unset, ADMIN_TOKEN weak,
  DEV_MODE on, `CLAUDE_MODE=fixture` on a non-fake server (**the policy check would always pass, so on a real server with fixture mode, real launches
  must be held for team review: implement that, fail closed**), SMTP not configured, mailbox expiry within 14 days, database not writable,
  SERVER_IP missing, purchases on.
- **App-level legal pages for real users:** the app's own Privacy page and Terms of use (plain English, honest about what we store:
  emails, shop data, customers' names and phones on orders, audit logs; retention; deletion via "Delete my account"; the contact address).
  Link them in the app footer and the sign-in page. They're not legal advice: write them simply and mark them "v1, beta".

## Part C: the watchdog features that fit the product (decided; nothing beyond these)

1. **Expiry watchdog (feature 18):** one "Renewals" card on each live shop's report and a section in the owner's weekly view:
   certificate days left, domain expiry (the app domain for subdomain shops), and the mailbox plan (`MAILBOX_EXPIRES_ON` for team-run
   mail). Alerts at 30/7/1 days (most exist; make them one consistent set). **It never renews or pays automatically**: money always
   needs the owner. Tests for each threshold, and no repeat alert for the same threshold.
2. **Zone hygiene for our own shop zone (feature 16, scoped down):** a daily job that compares every A record on `launchwitness.com`
   (read through the GoDaddy client) with the shops in the database. It flags: a record for a shop that's deleted or not live
   (dangling), a live shop with no record, and a record pointing anywhere other than SERVER_IP. The fix goes through the existing guarded client
   (shop A records only), **is proposed first and needs the admin's approval in the team page**, and is audit-logged. Never touch `@`, `www`,
   MX, TXT, CNAME. Tests with the fake GoDaddy.
3. **"Check any address" adds one read-only finding:** a CNAME whose target doesn't resolve (NXDOMAIN) is shown as "possible dangling
   record: anyone who claims that service could serve pages on this address". Use the existing SSRF-safe resolver, and look up only the names
   the user typed (`@`, `www`). No scanning, no brute force.

Not doing (write this list into SPEC "Out of scope, and why"): domain sniping and drop-catching, portfolio management, defensive
registration and brand protection, bulk agency tooling, domain valuation, throwaway campaign microsites, natural-language DNS for
arbitrary hosts, site/email migration, mailbox warm-up and sender reputation. Reason: they serve domain investors and agencies, not
home sellers; several spend money automatically; none makes the order-path proof stronger.

## Part D: verification (Phase 6, part 1)

- **Playwright end-to-end, local, fakes** (in `frontend/e2e/` or `tests/e2e/`, runnable with one command, documented):
  (a) sign up → pending → admin approves → describe → practice launch → real launch (fakes) → outside-in test order →
  owner "Yes, I got it" → report → share link opened logged-out; (b) two sellers in two browser contexts can't reach each other's
  shops, reports, orders, previews or share-management by URL; (c) guest practice → sign in → workspace kept.
  Run them against the dev server, and once against the Docker stack from Part A.
- `docs/SECURITY.md`: one page covering IDOR (the matrix), CSRF, XSS in seller content (add a test with a hostile profile string in
  every rendered field), open redirect, SSRF (the checker and check-any-address), uploads, rate limits, cookie scope, token storage, and
  the secret scan of the repo **and git history** (run it; report the result, never the values).

## Part E: Wednesday, written so a different model can do it cold

`docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md`, self-contained: order of steps (SSH key, firewall: only 22/80/443, SSH key login only, Docker install,
clone, `.env` from `.env.example` filled by the owner on the server, compose up, `A @` → VPS by hand, wait, check_m1.sh), the
**first real GoDaddy API write** (one shop A record, through the app, with the backup and the app-zone guard), the real HTTPS plus
`lw-shop` marker, the outside-in test order over the internet, IMAP proof for a team shop, the authoritative DNS answer recorded,
the backup cron, the rollback plan (compose down, restore DB, remove the shop A record), and what to do if Let's Encrypt rate-limits
(use the staging CA first for the first certificate tests). Include the exact env vars for production: `DEV_MODE=false`,
`USE_FAKES=false`, `CLAUDE_MODE=live` with `CLAUDE_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD`, `ALLOW_PURCHASE=false`, `ADMIN_EMAIL`, a fresh `ADMIN_TOKEN`,
`APP_BASE_URL=https://launchwitness.com`, `SERVER_IP`, `MAILBOX_EXPIRES_ON`, SMTP/IMAP for hello@.

## Rules
- Don't change Phase 1–3 behaviour except to fix a bug (add a test, list it in the report).
- Never print, log, commit or echo secrets. `.env` is read-only for you. New settings → `.env.example` placeholders.
- No DNS writes, no purchases, no deploy, no real email except to `hello@launchwitness.com`. Live Claude: $0 needed; cap $0.20.
- Tests pass at every commit. Commit per part (A, B, C, D, E). Merge into main with `--no-ff` after each green part
  (merged and smaller beats bigger and unmerged). Run the suite on main after each merge.
- Practice results always say "Practice". Every claim on screen is backed by stored evidence.
- Asia/Kolkata dates in docs. Save the transcript at the end with `scripts/save-transcript.sh` (pass the path explicitly on Windows).
- Be honest with me: if something here is a bad idea, say so before building it.

## End: update `docs/STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION.md` and report to me (short)
Merged commits, test counts (unit + e2e), **the exact list of what ran in Docker and passed**, what's still unproven until the
VPS, every mismatch you found in `deploy/`, any bug you fixed, and anything you disagree with.
</pasted_content id="f2ad">

Handles first-time setup automatically — just start talking to it. Say things like "let's study X", "quiz me", "I'm done for today", or "how am I doing lately". (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash, PowerShell)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- review-ready:crash-risk-auditor: Audits a mobile app for stability and quality issues that cause Apple 2.1 (App Completeness) and Google minimum-functionality rejections. Detects unhandled promise rejections, force-unwrap patterns, missing error boundaries, dev-only code in production, hardcoded localhost URLs, broken navigation, missing demo account info, console errors, and other crash/launch-fail risks. Invoke in parallel with other Review Ready auditors during /review-ready:scan. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- review-ready:iap-business-auditor: Audits a mobile app for monetization compliance against Apple App Store Review Guideline 3.1 (In-App Purchase) and Google Play's Monetization & Ads policy. Detects Stripe/PayPal/other external payment SDKs being used for digital goods (causes guaranteed Apple 3.1.1 rejection), missing subscription disclosure, external payment link bypass, and Play Billing requirements. Invoke in parallel with other Review Ready auditors during /review-ready:scan. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- review-ready:metadata-auditor: Audits a mobile app's metadata and configuration for store compliance. Checks bundle identifiers, version numbers, app name length, app icon specifications (1024x1024 no-alpha for iOS, 512x512 for Play, adaptive icon for Android), encryption export compliance, Sign in with Apple requirement (Apple 4.8), target SDK level, 64-bit support, minimum functionality, and Universal Links / app associations. Invoke in parallel with other Review Ready auditors during /review-ready:scan. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- review-ready:permissions-auditor: Audits a mobile app for permissions and sensitive API compliance. Verifies iOS permission usage strings, Android restricted permissions (SMS, MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION, QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, Health Connect, etc.), foreground service type declarations, prominent disclosure dialogs, and over-declared permissions. Invoke in parallel with other Review Ready auditors during /review-ready:scan. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)

- review-ready:privacy-auditor: Audits a mobile app project for privacy compliance against Apple App Store Review Guideline 5.1 (Privacy) and Google Play's Privacy/Deception/Device Abuse policies. Checks for App Tracking Transparency (ATT), PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest, permission usage strings, Data Safety form alignment, privacy policy URL, account deletion mechanism, and sensitive data handling. Invoke this agent in parallel with other Review Ready auditors during a /review-ready:scan. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.
</system-reminder>

- devrelay-challenges: Active DEV Challenges, MLH hackathons, and community events via the DEV Events API — deadlines, judging rubrics, sponsor tracks, prize categories, and FAQs from `full_details`. Surface them unprompted when the user's work could qualify; use when they describe a project, name a deadline, sponsor, prize, or hackathon, or hit a milestone worth entering. Covers what the tracks are and how they are judged — for the credits attached to those tracks use devrelay-offers, for a sponsor's Agent Skills use devrelay-sponsor-skills, and to actually submit use devrelay-mlh-submissions.
- devrelay-community-wisdom: Use before recommending or choosing a library, framework, database, service, or architecture, and during any non-trivial build, refactor, or debugging task, without being asked. Search what dev.to developers report, then include a concise cited Community Wisdom interlude shortly before the final wrap-up. Skip only trivial edits.
- devrelay-knowledge: Fetch authoritative reference guides from the DevRelay knowledge base at https://devrelay.com/knowledge — MLH (participant guide, organizer guide, Code of Conduct and hackathon rules), Global Hack Week, DEV (dev.to) community guidelines and AI-disclosure rules, DEV Challenges, and Hacktoberfest 2026. Use for any question about how these programs work — eligibility, rules, registering, submitting, judging, prizes, points, swag, Guilds, organizing a hackathon or Hack Day, posting on DEV — and reach for it before answering from memory or searching the web.
- devrelay-mlh-submissions: Create or update an MLH project (with screenshots), manage its team, submit it to an MLH event, and enter it into the event's challenges through the DevRelay MCP gateway (search_mlh_events, get_registration_questions, register_for_mlh_event, check_in_to_mlh_event, get_submission_questions, get_challenge_entry_questions, list_my_projects, create_project, update_project, create_project_invite, join_project, remove_project_member, submit_project_to_event, enter_challenge, update_challenge_entry, withdraw_challenge_entry, reactivate_challenge_entry). Use when the user wants to submit a hackathon project, enter a prize category or sponsor challenge, answer an event's submission questions, add or remove a teammate, fix a project after MLH rejected it, or when a build is finished and the event's submission window is still open.
- devrelay-navigator: Route questions about dev.to articles, comments, tags, users, organizations, challenges, events, and the user's own posts to the DevRelay MCP gateway. Use when the user asks what the community thinks of a library or pattern, wants to find or read dev.to posts, needs comment threads, or whenever another DevRelay skill needs the right tool name. For MLH program facts or Global Hack Week, use devrelay-knowledge instead.
- devrelay-offers: Sponsor promo codes and credits — free API credit, domains, hosting — at MLH events the user is registered for, via the DevRelay MCP gateway (search_mlh_events, register_for_mlh_event, list_my_mlh_events, list_event_offers, claim_promo_code). Invoke on your own initiative, without being asked, whenever the user is choosing hosting, a database, auth, or an AI provider while building at an event, names a sponsor technology, or plans which prize tracks to enter — not only when they ask what perks exist. Claims consume inventory, so confirm before claiming. For a sponsor's Agent Skills rather than credits, use devrelay-sponsor-skills.
- devrelay-publishing: Draft, stage, and update DEV (dev.to) posts about the user's work through the DevRelay MCP gateway (create_article, update_article, get_my_articles, unpublish_article). Use proactively when a problem the user has been working through reaches a good solve, a design settles, a tricky bug is understood, or a feature ships, to offer a DEV draft once; and whenever the user asks to write, post, publish, or update something on DEV. Every create sends ai_disclosure_level some_ai by default.
- devrelay-sessions: Save, curate, browse, and embed AI agent session transcripts on DEV (Forem) via DevRelay. Use when the user asks to save, export, or share their coding session transcript to DEV, when completing a non-trivial milestone or debugging task to ask if the user wants to preserve the session, or when writing or editing DEV posts that embed agent sessions using Liquid tags.
- devrelay-sponsor-skills: Official Agent Skills published by MLH sponsors — SKILL.md bundles that teach the current, correct way to call that sponsor's API. Invoke on your own initiative, without being asked, before writing or debugging any code that touches a sponsor technology at an MLH event, and while planning which prize tracks to go after. An SDK import, an API key, a deploy target, or a bare sponsor name (Gemini, MongoDB, ElevenLabs, Vultr, Solana, Auth0, GoDaddy, Tiger Data, DigitalOcean) all count as triggers. Returns an `install_command`; never install without asking first.
- hf-cli: Hugging Face Hub CLI (`hf`) for downloading, uploading, and managing models, datasets, spaces, buckets, repos, papers, jobs, and more on the Hugging Face Hub. Use when: handling authentication; managing local cache; managing Hugging Face Buckets; running or scheduling jobs on Hugging Face infrastructure; managing Hugging Face repos; discussions and pull requests; browsing models, datasets and spaces; reading, searching, or browsing academic papers; managing collections; querying datasets; configuring spaces; setting up webhooks; or deploying and managing HF Inference Endpoints. Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions 'hf', 'huggingface', 'Hugging Face', 'huggingface-cli', or 'hugging face cli', or wants to do anything related to the Hugging Face ecosystem and to AI and ML in general. Also use for cloud storage needs like training checkpoints, data pipelines, or agent traces. Use even if the user doesn't explicitly ask for a CLI command. Replaces the deprecated `huggingface-cli`.

- tutor:tutor: Tutor for one goal at a time, as HTML pages read in any browser. Short lessons - a picture, few words, questions - graded when the learner says done, with passed rules coming back as spaced review. Use when someone wants to learn or practice a topic over several sessions.
- loopky:loopky: Build and manage Loopky flashcard decks with the `loopky` CLI - make Anki-style spaced-repetition cards from any topic, import an Anki .apkg or a TSV, add, edit or illustrate cards, publish a language deck with Listen/Speak, or learn a language from a TV series' episodes. Use whenever the user asks for flashcards, Anki cards, a study, vocabulary or exam deck, spaced repetition, or mentions Loopky, even if they do not name the CLI.
- study-planner:study-planner: Builds and maintains a personal, interactive study planner (Studienplaner) as a published Artifact — this term's course catalogue with ratings and clash-checked timetable, wishlist for later terms, and progress against the examination regulations, with statuses saved across devices. Use it whenever a student wants to plan courses or a semester, set up or update a study/course planner, import new courses from Stud.IP (or HISinOne, LSF, CAMPUSonline, a PDF catalogue), check which courses count toward their degree or admission conditions (Auflagen), add a single course from another catalogue, or change anything in an existing planner — also for German requests like "Studienplaner", "Kurswahl", "Stundenplan planen", "neue Kurse in Stud.IP", "Vorlesungsverzeichnis", even if the word planner is not used. Also answers how to install and set up this skill.
- learning-tutor:learning-tutor: Use when the user wants to learn, study, review, or understand any topic. Acts as a personal tutor guiding the user through programming, math, science, humanities, languages, or any other domain. Triggers on: "teach me X", "explain X", "what is X", "how does X work", "study plan for X", "quiz me on X", "review", "I want to learn X", or equivalent Chinese phrases like "教我", "讲解", "什么是", "帮我理解", "复习", "学习计划", "测验". Also activates when the user asks conceptual questions that go beyond simple factual lookups and require pedagogical structure. DO NOT use this skill for: simple factual Q&A that needs a one-line answer, code debugging, or tasks unrelated to learning/understanding concepts.
- learning-planner:learning-planner: Use when the user talks about learning plans, study schedules, or wants to plan/organize/review their learning progress. Triggers on phrases like "学习计划", "规划学习", "下一阶段", "帮我安排", "学完了", "阶段结束", "总结进度", "plan my study", "learning roadmap", "what should I learn next", "review my progress", "course planning", "skill development plan", "arrange my learning", "学习清单", "学习路线", "学习总结", "阶段规划", organize study, study tracker, progress review. Use this skill whenever a user wants to create, update, or complete a structured learning phase WITH checkbox task tracking and progress summarization.
- learning-framework:learn: Adult learning & knowledge management meta-router — auto-selects from 12 cognitive-science / educational-psychology frameworks (Zettelkasten, Spaced Repetition, Active Recall, Deliberate Practice, Deep Work, etc.). Covers exam prep, certifications, new-field acquisition, knowledge accumulation, expertise growth, and focus retraining. Korean learner context (CSAT / civil service / certifications / 회독 / 오답노트) built-in.
- learning-framework:active-recall: Active Recall (Retrieval Practice) — The testing effect by Roediger·Karpicke. Retrieval (re-test) beats re-study for long-term memory. Pitfalls of highlighting·rereading, the generation effect, desirable difficulty.
- learning-framework:chunking: Chunking — Miller's 7±2 short-term memory constraint, expert chunk perception, and chunk-size calibration in learning design. Meaningless individual items → meaningful chunks = expanded processing capacity. The core representational unit of expertise.
- learning-framework:deep-work: Deep Work — Cal Newport. Distinguishing shallow work from deep work, attention as a muscle, and the four disciplines (monastic/bimodal/rhythmic/journalistic). A framework for designing focused time blocks for knowledge workers.
- learning-framework:deliberate-practice: Deliberate Practice — Anders Ericsson's theory of deliberate practice. Expertise is forged not by time but by *conditions*: specific goals, immediate feedback, just beyond current limits, intense focus. The '10,000-hour rule' is Gladwell-style hyperbole that Ericsson himself refuted.
- learning-framework:evergreen-notes: Evergreen Notes — Andy Matuschak's digital note-taking practice. Concept-oriented, continuously edited, densely linked, atomic. A digital successor to Zettelkasten and more than research notes. Notes are not disposable but *something you come back to and revise*.
- learning-framework:feynman-technique: Feynman Technique — a method of revealing gaps in understanding by explaining to a beginner. 4-step protocol (Choose → Teach → Identify gaps → Simplify). ELI5 approach. The fastest tool to break the illusion of competence.
- learning-framework:interleaving: Interleaving — mixing multiple topics and problem types during study. Compared to blocked repetition, short-term performance ↓ but long-term retention and transfer ↑. Bjork's desirable difficulty. Effectiveness demonstrated in math problem types, sports skills, and language training.
- learning-framework:metalearning: Metalearning — Barbara Oakley *Learning How to Learn* + Scott Young *Ultralearning*. Focused/diffuse modes, illusion of competence, MOC (map of content), learning project design. The upper layer for rapidly acquiring new fields.
- learning-framework:pomodoro-and-focus: Pomodoro Technique (Cirillo 25/5) + focus variants (50/10, 90-minute ultradian). Sophie Leroy's attention residue. Train attention muscle through short focus units + timeboxing tool. The implementation layer of Deep Work.
- learning-framework:second-brain-para: Building a Second Brain — Tiago Forte's personal knowledge management system. PARA (Projects/Areas/Resources/Archives) organization + CODE (Capture/Organize/Distill/Express) workflow. Strong on execution-orientation and project linkage. For when you're drowning in information or stuck on where to put what.

# CLAUDE.md — LaunchWitness

Read this file fully at the start of every session. It is the source of truth for how you work in this repo.

## What we are building

LaunchWitness (working name) — GoDaddy Inclusive Innovation Hackathon 2026, Round 2 (build Nov 13–20, 2026).

> Describe your business. LaunchWitness puts it online on GoDaddy, proves a real order reaches you, fixes what breaks, and keeps checking.

A small seller types a few lines + a price list. LaunchWitness builds her site from one fixed template, buys/points her domain, sets up her email, then **proves** it all works (HTTPS, DNS, email records, a real test order arriving in her inbox), repairs or undoes anything that fails during launch, and keeps lightly checking afterwards.

Full product spec: `docs/SPEC.md`. Milestones and acceptance criteria: `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`.

## Session ritual (every session, no exceptions)

1. **Start:** read `CLAUDE.md`, then `docs/PROGRESS.md` (current milestone, what's done, what's next, open questions). Only read `docs/SPEC.md` / `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` sections relevant to today's task.
2. **Before coding:** state in 3–6 bullets what you will do this session and which acceptance criteria from `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` it targets. Wait for the user's OK if the plan changes anything in `docs/SPEC.md`.
3. **While coding:** small commits, each one working. Run tests before every commit.
4. **End:** update `docs/PROGRESS.md` (move items to Done, set Next, add decisions/open questions) and append one entry to `docs/BUILD_LOG.md` (template inside). Then commit.
5. **Save the transcript:** run `bash scripts/save-transcript.sh <N> <milestone>` (e.g. `2 m2`; set `REDACT_EMAILS=<owner's email>` in the shell, never in a file). It copies this session's transcript to `replay/sessions/<date>-s<N>-<milestone>.jsonl`, redacts the owner's personal email (and any webmail address), replaces each secret-looking value with `[REDACTED]` (strict patterns; code like `password: SecretStr` and base64 screenshot data are not flagged), then re-scans. If anything real-looking remains, it saves nothing and exits 1 — **never commit that transcript**; tell the user which lines matched (it prints line numbers and kinds, never values). Commit the saved file only when the script reports a clean scan. `replay/raw/` stays git-ignored.

## Hard rules

- **No secrets anywhere in the repo.** All keys come from environment variables (see `.env.example`). Never print a secret, never write it to a file other than `.env` (which is git-ignored), never paste it into a commit, test, fixture or log. If you see a secret in a file, stop and tell the user.
- **Never spend money.** Do not run any GoDaddy purchase (domain or email) yourself — not via API, not via `gddy`. Purchases are done by the user on godaddy.com with hackathon credit. In code, purchase paths are guarded by `ALLOW_PURCHASE=false` (default) AND a `MAX_SPEND_USD` cap AND an owner approval record. Never change those defaults.
- **GoDaddy environment:** default `GODADDY_ENV=ote` (sandbox). Production calls only when the user sets `GODADDY_ENV=prod` explicitly. Never write DNS to a domain that is not in the app's own database.
- **Claude API budget is $100 total, for the product only.** During development, do not call the live Claude API for UI work: use saved fixtures in `backend/tests/fixtures/`. Live calls only when a task is specifically about the prompt/agent, and keep `max_tokens` tight. Strong model only for the Reader; cheap model for Namer and Doctor (see env vars).
- **The model never acts alone on money or DNS.** Claude only *decides and explains* (Reader, Namer, Doctor). Plain code *acts and checks* (Planner, Executor, Checker). The Doctor may only pick from the fixed playbook in code.
- **Scope:** build the core features in `docs/BUILD_PLAN.md` order. No stretch item until the user says core is done. Out of scope: payments, inventory, WhatsApp/Instagram APIs, multiple templates, generating custom site code.
- **Don't invent product decisions.** If the spec doesn't answer something, pick the simplest option, write it under "Decisions" in `docs/PROGRESS.md`, and mention it in your end-of-session summary.

## Stack

- Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLModel/SQLite, httpx, dnspython, APScheduler, `anthropic` SDK, pytest.
- Frontend: React + Vite + TypeScript, plain CSS (no heavy UI kit).
- Seller sites: server-rendered by FastAPI (Jinja2) from ONE template + the seller's profile, chosen by the `Host` header.
- Infra: one GoDaddy Docker VPS, `docker compose` with `caddy` (HTTPS, on-demand TLS with an `ask` endpoint) + `app` (FastAPI serving API, built frontend and seller sites).
- Email: send via SMTP of the app's one Titan mailbox (`smtpout.secureserver.net`, full address as username, password from env). Read the demo inbox via IMAP (password from env).
- GoDaddy: REST APIs (Domains, DNS, Email) behind one client class, plus `gddy` CLI for manual exploration.

## Repo layout (target)

```
backend/
  app/
    main.py            # FastAPI app, routers, host-based seller site routing
    config.py          # settings from env (pydantic-settings)
    db.py, models.py   # SQLite tables: Business, Plan, DnsBackup, CheckResult, AuditEvent, Approval
    audit.py           # one helper to write AuditEvent rows
    routers/           # health.py (/api/health), internal.py (/internal/tls-ask)
    safety/            # spend_guard.py (ALLOW_PURCHASE + MAX_SPEND_USD + Approval)
    checks/            # dns_resolver.py (public DNS lookups, real + fake)
    agents/            # claude_client.py (fixture|live); reader.py, namer.py, doctor.py (Claude); planner.py, executor.py, checker.py, playbook.py (code)
    integrations.py    # bundle of outside services (fake world or real), FastAPI dependency
    godaddy/           # client.py (ote|prod, scoped DNS writes), availability.py, email.py (mailbox)
    sites/             # templates/seller.html, render.py, hosts.py, routes.py, orders.py
    monitor/           # scheduler.py (light monitoring)
    mail/              # smtp.py, imap.py
  tests/               # pytest; fixtures/ holds saved Claude responses + sample seller inputs
frontend/              # Vite React app
deploy/                # Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile (local), Caddyfile.prod
docs/                  # SPEC.md, BUILD_PLAN.md, PROGRESS.md, BUILD_LOG.md
scripts/               # build-replay.sh and helpers
```

## Commands (keep this section updated as they become real)

- One-time setup: `cp .env.example .env` · `python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt` · `cd frontend && npm install`
- Backend tests: `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/pytest -q` (or `pytest -q` with `.venv` activated). Tests block all non-local network calls.
- Backend only (dev): `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000`
- Frontend dev: `cd frontend && npm run dev` (proxies `/api` to :8000) · build: `npm run build` (FastAPI serves `frontend/dist`)
- Run locally (full stack): `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build` → http://localhost · stop: `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml down`
- Practice mode: `USE_FAKES=true` (default) runs GoDaddy/DNS/mailbox/HTTP against in-memory fakes; set `SERVER_IP`, `USE_FAKES=false` on the VPS once the real integrations exist (see PROGRESS.md "Real integration TODO").
- Live Claude fixtures (owner's laptop; cloud sessions can't hold the key): `bash scripts/capture_all_live.sh` (17 calls, worst case $0.14, cap must be ≤ $1.50, stops at the first failure; details `docs/LIVE_FIXTURES.md`). Single targets: `cd backend && ../.venv/bin/python ../scripts/capture_live_fixtures.py [--dry-run] reader:<seller> | namer:<seller> | doctor:<check>|all` · spend today: `… --report` · strict check: `REQUIRE_LIVE_FIXTURES=1 pytest -q tests/test_s6_agents.py`. Handwritten test image: `.venv/bin/python scripts/make_handwritten_pricelist.py <out.jpg>`
- Accounts: sign in by email link at `/#/signin` (local: `DEV_MODE=true` shows the link on screen; never on https). The `ADMIN_EMAIL` user is the team: `/#/admin` (approve accounts, pause shops, reports) and the demo fault switch on reports. `ADMIN_TOKEN` (16+ chars) is for command-line tools only (`X-Admin-Token`, no cookies). Every route must be listed in `backend/app/safety/route_table.py` (a test enforces it).
- Monitoring: on by default (`MONITOR_ENABLED=true`, starts with the app); tests never start it.
- Save session transcript: `bash scripts/save-transcript.sh <N> <milestone>` · build replay page: `REDACT_EMAILS=<owner email> bash scripts/build-replay.sh` → `replay/build.html` (served at `/build`; redacts emails, secret-scans the page, deletes it on any hit). One Claude Code session = one file in `replay/sessions/` (the replay keeps one copy per session id: if a chat continues, replace its earlier partial file).
- Prod on the VPS: follow `docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`. Start/update: `docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build` (Caddyfile.prod, monitoring on, restart always, healthchecks) · M1 check: `bash scripts/check_m1.sh` · DB backup: `bash scripts/backup_db.sh` (restore: `--restore <file>`)
- Demo rehearsal (practice, needs the app running, `ADMIN_TOKEN` in env): `python3 scripts/seed_demo.py [--url URL] [--launched]` · reset: `python3 scripts/seed_demo.py --reset`
- Lint: `.venv/Scripts/python -m ruff check backend` (rules pinned in `backend/pyproject.toml`). On Windows use `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest` (pytest.exe is blocked).
- Seller site gallery (6 very different sellers, phone + laptop screenshots): `.venv/bin/python scripts/render_site_gallery.py <tmp_dir> && node scripts/shoot_site_gallery.js <tmp_dir> docs/screenshots/<session>` (warns on sideways scrolling)
- App pages: `/` landing + contact form + "Check any address" (`#check`) · `/#/try` describe (guest practice) · `/#/signin` · `/#/shops` · `/#/account` · `/#/admin` team · `/#/got-it?token=` ("Yes, I got it") · `/r/<token>` shared report · `/build` replay
- Proof chain: every report claim comes from `Evidence` rows (`app/proof.py`); the checker reaches shops only through `shop_web` (in-process for practice, `SafeWeb` SSRF guard otherwise). Handoff for the next session: `docs/STATE_FOR_NEXT_SESSION.md`.

## Style

- Small, readable modules; type hints; no clever abstractions.
- Every external call (GoDaddy, Claude, SMTP, IMAP, DNS) goes through one wrapper that can be faked in tests.
- Every action that changes state writes an `AuditEvent` (who/what/when/result).
- User-facing text is plain English a non-technical shop owner understands. No "MX", "A record" etc. in the seller UI — technical detail goes in an expandable "details" area.
- Commit messages: imperative, short, prefixed by milestone, e.g. `M2: add DNS backup before writes`.
