#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stack acceptance check. Two places, same checks:
#
#   bash scripts/check_m1.sh            # ON THE VPS, from the repo, stack running (reads .env, never prints secrets)
#   bash scripts/check_m1.sh --local    # this computer: the production-like Docker stack (deploy/README.md)
#   EXTERNAL_SUBJECT="hello from my gmail" bash scripts/check_m1.sh   # VPS: also look for your external test email
#
# Checks: DNS (VPS: `A @` and each live shop's own A record; there is NO wildcard), HTTPS + certificate + HSTS +
# http->https, /api/health and its warnings (mailbox expiry), /internal/* blocked from outside on every host but
# working inside the network, the shop-host guard, the session cookie's flags over https, the ADMIN_EMAIL user,
# exactly one app process, the mailbox (SMTP/IMAP; local: Mailpit), a contact-form message arriving, and that
# the SMTP password is in no tracked file or commit. Exit code = number of failures.

set -uo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO"
FAILS=0
pass() { printf '  \033[32mPASS\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { printf '  \033[31mFAIL\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); }
warn() { printf '  \033[33mWARN\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; }
info() { printf '        %s\n' "$1"; }

LOCAL=false
[ "${1:-}" = "--local" ] && LOCAL=true

# Read one value from .env without printing it (no `source`: values may contain spaces/symbols).
envval() { grep -E "^$1=" .env 2>/dev/null | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2- | sed -e 's/[[:space:]]#.*$//' -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//"; }

if $LOCAL; then
  COMPOSE=(docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml)
  APP_DOMAIN=launchwitness.localhost
  SERVER_IP=127.0.0.1
  CA="$(mktemp)"
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" cp caddy:/data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt "$CA" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "FAIL: can't read Caddy's local CA (is the local stack up? see deploy/README.md)"; exit 1; }
  CURL=(curl -sS --max-time 20 --cacert "$CA")
  curl --version | grep -qi schannel && CURL+=(--ssl-no-revoke)  # Windows curl: no revocation list for a local CA
else
  [ -f .env ] || { echo "FAIL: no .env in $REPO (see docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md)"; exit 1; }
  COMPOSE=(docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml)
  APP_DOMAIN="$(envval APP_DOMAIN)"
  SERVER_IP="$(envval SERVER_IP)"
  CURL=(curl -sS --max-time 20)
fi
BASE="https://$APP_DOMAIN"
echo "Stack check for $BASE (server $SERVER_IP)$($LOCAL && echo ', LOCAL stack')"

if [ -z "$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q app 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  fail "the app container isn't running"; echo "$FAILS failure(s)"; exit "$FAILS"
fi
inapp() { "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T app python - "$@"; }

# ---------- 1. DNS ----------
echo "1. Addresses (DNS)"
if $LOCAL; then
  info "(local: *.localhost always means this computer; skipped)"
elif [ -z "$APP_DOMAIN" ] || [ "$APP_DOMAIN" = "localhost" ]; then
  fail "APP_DOMAIN is not set to your real domain in .env"
else
  ip="$(getent ahostsv4 "$APP_DOMAIN" | awk 'NR==1{print $1}')"
  [ -n "$ip" ] && [ "$ip" = "$SERVER_IP" ] && pass "DNS: $APP_DOMAIN -> $ip" \
    || fail "DNS: $APP_DOMAIN -> ${ip:-nothing} (want $SERVER_IP; DNS can take up to an hour)"
  if command -v dig >/dev/null; then
    ns="$(dig +short NS "$APP_DOMAIN" | head -n1)"
    auth="$(dig +short A "$APP_DOMAIN" @"${ns:-ns01.domaincontrol.com}" | head -n1)"
    [ "$auth" = "$SERVER_IP" ] && pass "authoritative answer from ${ns%?}: $auth" || fail "authoritative answer from ${ns:-?}: ${auth:-nothing}"
  fi
fi
SHOPS="$(inapp <<'PY' 2>/dev/null
from sqlmodel import Session, select
from app.db import get_engine
from app.models import Business
with Session(get_engine()) as s:
    for b in s.exec(select(Business).where(Business.status == "live", Business.practice == False, Business.paused == False)).all():  # noqa: E712
        if b.subdomain:
            print(b.subdomain)
PY
)"
SHOP="$(echo "$SHOPS" | head -n1 | tr -d '\r')"
info "live real shops: $(echo "$SHOPS" | grep -c . || true)"
if ! $LOCAL; then
  for s in $SHOPS; do
    ip="$(getent ahostsv4 "$s.$APP_DOMAIN" | awk 'NR==1{print $1}')"
    [ "$ip" = "$SERVER_IP" ] && pass "DNS: $s.$APP_DOMAIN -> $ip (its own A record)" || fail "DNS: $s.$APP_DOMAIN -> ${ip:-nothing}"
  done
  nope="$(getent ahostsv4 "lw-no-such-shop-$RANDOM.$APP_DOMAIN" | awk 'NR==1{print $1}')"
  [ -z "$nope" ] && pass "no wildcard: an unused name doesn't resolve" || warn "an unused name resolves to $nope (a wildcard record exists? we decided per-shop records only)"
fi

# ---------- 2. HTTPS ----------
echo "2. Website over HTTPS"
if body="$("${CURL[@]}" "$BASE/api/health" 2>&1)" && echo "$body" | grep -q '"ok":true'; then
  pass "$BASE/api/health with a valid certificate"
  echo "$body" | grep -q '"warnings"' && warn "health warnings: $(echo "$body" | sed -e 's/.*"warnings":\[//' -e 's/\].*//')" \
    || pass "health: no warnings"
else
  fail "$BASE/api/health: ${body:0:200}"
fi
hsts="$("${CURL[@]}" -o /dev/null -D - "$BASE/" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | grep -i '^strict-transport-security:')"
[ -n "$hsts" ] && pass "HSTS on the app ($hsts)" || fail "no Strict-Transport-Security header on $BASE"
redir="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' --max-time 10 "http://$APP_DOMAIN/")"
case "$redir" in 30[178]\ https://*) pass "http -> https ($redir)";; *) fail "http://$APP_DOMAIN/ answered '$redir' (want a redirect to https)";; esac
if ! $LOCAL; then
  end="$(echo | openssl s_client -connect "$APP_DOMAIN:443" -servername "$APP_DOMAIN" 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate -issuer 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
  [ -n "$end" ] && info "certificate: $end"
fi

# ---------- 3. /internal and the shop-host guard ----------
echo "3. Internal endpoints and shop hosts"
bad=""
for p in "/internal/tls-ask?domain=$APP_DOMAIN" "/internal" "/INTERNAL/tls-ask?domain=x" "/internal%2ftls-ask?domain=$APP_DOMAIN" "//internal/tls-ask?domain=$APP_DOMAIN"; do
  code="$("${CURL[@]}" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$BASE$p")"
  [ "$code" = "404" ] || bad="$bad $p=$code"
done
[ -z "$bad" ] && pass "/internal/* answers 404 from outside (5 spellings)" || fail "/internal reachable from outside:$bad"
inside="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T caddy wget -qO- "http://app:8000/internal/tls-ask?domain=$APP_DOMAIN" 2>&1)"
echo "$inside" | grep -q '"ok":true' && pass "inside the network Caddy's ask works for $APP_DOMAIN" || fail "tls-ask inside the network: ${inside:0:120}"
unknown="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T caddy wget -qO- "http://app:8000/internal/tls-ask?domain=lw-nobody.$APP_DOMAIN" 2>&1)"
echo "$unknown" | grep -q '404' && pass "no certificate for a shop that doesn't exist" || fail "tls-ask said yes to an unknown shop: ${unknown:0:120}"
if [ -n "$SHOP" ]; then
  SB="https://$SHOP.$APP_DOMAIN"
  page="$("${CURL[@]}" "$SB/" 2>&1)"
  echo "$page" | grep -q 'name="lw-shop"' && pass "$SB opens over HTTPS with its lw-shop marker" || fail "$SB: no lw-shop marker"
  bad=""
  for p in /api/health /internal/tls-ask /build /r/x /assets/x.js; do
    code="$("${CURL[@]}" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$SB$p")"; [ "$code" = "404" ] || bad="$bad $p=$code"
  done
  [ -z "$bad" ] && pass "shop host serves no app paths (/api /internal /build /r /assets: 404)" || fail "shop host answered:$bad"
else
  info "(no live real shop yet: shop-host checks skipped)"
fi

# ---------- 4. Accounts: session cookie over https, the admin user ----------
echo "4. Accounts"
admin="$(inapp <<'PY' 2>&1
from sqlmodel import Session, select
from app.config import get_settings
from app.db import get_engine
from app.models import User
s = get_settings()
with Session(get_engine()) as db:
    u = db.exec(select(User).where(User.email == s.admin_email.strip().lower())).first() if s.admin_email else None
    print("ADMIN", "unset" if not s.admin_email else ("ok" if u and u.role == "admin" and u.status == "approved" else "missing"))
    print("DEVMODE", s.dev_mode)
    print("MAILBOX", s.mailbox_expires_on or "unset")
PY
)"
case "$(echo "$admin" | awk '/^ADMIN/{print $2}')" in
  ok) pass "the ADMIN_EMAIL user exists, approved, role admin";;
  unset) fail "ADMIN_EMAIL is not set";;
  *) fail "the ADMIN_EMAIL user is missing or not admin";;
esac
[ "$(echo "$admin" | awk '/^DEVMODE/{print $2}')" = "False" ] && pass "DEV_MODE is off" || fail "DEV_MODE is on"
mb="$(echo "$admin" | awk '/^MAILBOX/{print $2}')"
if [ "$mb" = "unset" ]; then $LOCAL && info "MAILBOX_EXPIRES_ON unset (fine locally)" || fail "MAILBOX_EXPIRES_ON is not set (health can't warn before hello@ lapses)"
else pass "MAILBOX_EXPIRES_ON = $mb (health warns 14 days ahead)"; fi
# A one-time sign-in token for the admin, made inside the app and used once over https, then signed out.
# Nothing is emailed. The token never reaches the screen.
TOKEN="$(inapp <<'PY' 2>/dev/null
from sqlmodel import Session
from app.accounts import issue_token
from app.config import get_settings
from app.db import get_engine
s = get_settings()
if s.admin_email:
    with Session(get_engine()) as db:
        print(issue_token(db, s.admin_email.strip().lower(), "login", visitor="check_m1"))
PY
)"
TOKEN="$(echo "$TOKEN" | tail -n1 | tr -d '\r')"
if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
  hdrs="$(mktemp)"
  resp="$("${CURL[@]}" -D "$hdrs" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Origin: $BASE" \
    --data-binary @- "$BASE/api/auth/confirm" <<<"{\"token\":\"$TOKEN\"}")"
  unset TOKEN
  cookie="$(tr -d '\r' < "$hdrs" | grep -i '^set-cookie: __Host-lw_session=' | head -n1)"
  flags="$(echo "$cookie" | sed -E 's/^set-cookie: __Host-lw_session=[^;]*//I')"  # the value is never shown
  okc=true
  for f in "secure" "httponly" "samesite=lax" "path=/"; do echo "$flags" | grep -qi "$f" || okc=false; done
  echo "$flags" | grep -qi "domain=" && okc=false
  $okc && pass "__Host-lw_session over https:$flags" || fail "session cookie flags wrong or missing:${flags:-(no __Host-lw_session cookie)}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stack acceptance check. Two places, same checks:
#
#   bash scripts/check_m1.sh            # ON THE VPS, from the repo, stack running (reads .env, never prints secrets)
#   bash scripts/check_m1.sh --local    # this computer: the production-like Docker stack (deploy/README.md)
#   EXTERNAL_SUBJECT="hello from my gmail" bash scripts/check_m1.sh   # VPS: also look for your external test email
#
# Checks: DNS (VPS: `A @` and each live shop's own A record; there is NO wildcard), HTTPS + certificate + HSTS +
# http->https, /api/health and its warnings (mailbox expiry), /internal/* blocked from outside on every host but
# working inside the network, the shop-host guard, the session cookie's flags over https, the ADMIN_EMAIL user,
# exactly one app process, the mailbox (SMTP/IMAP; local: Mailpit), a contact-form message arriving, and that
# the SMTP password is in no tracked file or commit. Exit code = number of failures.

set -uo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO"
FAILS=0
pass() { printf '  \033[32mPASS\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { printf '  \033[31mFAIL\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); }
warn() { printf '  \033[33mWARN\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; }
info() { printf '        %s\n' "$1"; }

LOCAL=false
[ "${1:-}" = "--local" ] && LOCAL=true

# Read one value from .env without printing it (no `source`: values may contain spaces/symbols).
envval() { grep -E "^$1=" .env 2>/dev/null | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2- | sed -e 's/[[:space:]]#.*$//' -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//"; }

if $LOCAL; then
  COMPOSE=(docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml)
  APP_DOMAIN=launchwitness.localhost
  SERVER_IP=127.0.0.1
  CA="$(mktemp)"
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" cp caddy:/data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt "$CA" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "FAIL: can't read Caddy's local CA (is the local stack up? see deploy/README.md)"; exit 1; }
  CURL=(curl -sS --max-time 20 --cacert "$CA")
  curl --version | grep -qi schannel && CURL+=(--ssl-no-revoke)  # Windows curl: no revocation list for a local CA
else
  [ -f .env ] || { echo "FAIL: no .env in $REPO (see docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md)"; exit 1; }
  COMPOSE=(docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml)
  APP_DOMAIN="$(envval APP_DOMAIN)"
  SERVER_IP="$(envval SERVER_IP)"
  CURL=(curl -sS --max-time 20)
fi
BASE="https://$APP_DOMAIN"
echo "Stack check for $BASE (server $SERVER_IP)$($LOCAL && echo ', LOCAL stack')"

if [ -z "$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q app 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  fail "the app container isn't running"; echo "$FAILS failure(s)"; exit "$FAILS"
fi
inapp() { "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T app python - "$@"; }

# ---------- 1. DNS ----------
echo "1. Addresses (DNS)"
if $LOCAL; then
  info "(local: *.localhost always means this computer; skipped)"
elif [ -z "$APP_DOMAIN" ] || [ "$APP_DOMAIN" = "localhost" ]; then
  fail "APP_DOMAIN is not set to your real domain in .env"
else
  ip="$(getent ahostsv4 "$APP_DOMAIN" | awk 'NR==1{print $1}')"
  [ -n "$ip" ] && [ "$ip" = "$SERVER_IP" ] && pass "DNS: $APP_DOMAIN -> $ip" \
    || fail "DNS: $APP_DOMAIN -> ${ip:-nothing} (want $SERVER_IP; DNS can take up to an hour)"
  if command -v dig >/dev/null; then
    ns="$(dig +short NS "$APP_DOMAIN" | head -n1)"
    auth="$(dig +short A "$APP_DOMAIN" @"${ns:-ns01.domaincontrol.com}" | head -n1)"
    [ "$auth" = "$SERVER_IP" ] && pass "authoritative answer from ${ns%?}: $auth" || fail "authoritative answer from ${ns:-?}: ${auth:-nothing}"
  fi
fi
SHOPS="$(inapp <<'PY' 2>/dev/null
from sqlmodel import Session, select
from app.db import get_engine
from app.models import Business
with Session(get_engine()) as s:
    for b in s.exec(select(Business).where(Business.status == "live", Business.practice == False, Business.paused == False)).all():  # noqa: E712
        if b.subdomain:
            print(b.subdomain)
PY
)"
SHOP="$(echo "$SHOPS" | head -n1 | tr -d '\r')"
info "live real shops: $(echo "$SHOPS" | grep -c . || true)"
if ! $LOCAL; then
  for s in $SHOPS; do
    ip="$(getent ahostsv4 "$s.$APP_DOMAIN" | awk 'NR==1{print $1}')"
    [ "$ip" = "$SERVER_IP" ] && pass "DNS: $s.$APP_DOMAIN -> $ip (its own A record)" || fail "DNS: $s.$APP_DOMAIN -> ${ip:-nothing}"
  done
  nope="$(getent ahostsv4 "lw-no-such-shop-$RANDOM.$APP_DOMAIN" | awk 'NR==1{print $1}')"
  [ -z "$nope" ] && pass "no wildcard: an unused name doesn't resolve" || warn "an unused name resolves to $nope (a wildcard record exists? we decided per-shop records only)"
fi

# ---------- 2. HTTPS ----------
echo "2. Website over HTTPS"
if body="$("${CURL[@]}" "$BASE/api/health" 2>&1)" && echo "$body" | grep -q '"ok":true'; then
  pass "$BASE/api/health with a valid certificate"
  echo "$body" | grep -q '"warnings"' && warn "health warnings: $(echo "$body" | sed -e 's/.*"warnings":\[//' -e 's/\].*//')" \
    || pass "health: no warnings"
else
  fail "$BASE/api/health: ${body:0:200}"
fi
hsts="$("${CURL[@]}" -o /dev/null -D - "$BASE/" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | grep -i '^strict-transport-security:')"
[ -n "$hsts" ] && pass "HSTS on the app ($hsts)" || fail "no Strict-Transport-Security header on $BASE"
redir="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' --max-time 10 "http://$APP_DOMAIN/")"
case "$redir" in 30[178]\ https://*) pass "http -> https ($redir)";; *) fail "http://$APP_DOMAIN/ answered '$redir' (want a redirect to https)";; esac
if ! $LOCAL; then
  end="$(echo | openssl s_client -connect "$APP_DOMAIN:443" -servername "$APP_DOMAIN" 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate -issuer 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
  [ -n "$end" ] && info "certificate: $end"
fi

# ---------- 3. /internal and the shop-host guard ----------
echo "3. Internal endpoints and shop hosts"
bad=""
for p in "/internal/tls-ask?domain=$APP_DOMAIN" "/internal" "/INTERNAL/tls-ask?domain=x" "/internal%2ftls-ask?domain=$APP_DOMAIN" "//internal/tls-ask?domain=$APP_DOMAIN"; do
  code="$("${CURL[@]}" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$BASE$p")"
  [ "$code" = "404" ] || bad="$bad $p=$code"
done
[ -z "$bad" ] && pass "/internal/* answers 404 from outside (5 spellings)" || fail "/internal reachable from outside:$bad"
inside="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T caddy wget -qO- "http://app:8000/internal/tls-ask?domain=$APP_DOMAIN" 2>&1)"
echo "$inside" | grep -q '"ok":true' && pass "inside the network Caddy's ask works for $APP_DOMAIN" || fail "tls-ask inside the network: ${inside:0:120}"
unknown="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T caddy wget -qO- "http://app:8000/internal/tls-ask?domain=lw-nobody.$APP_DOMAIN" 2>&1)"
echo "$unknown" | grep -q '404' && pass "no certificate for a shop that doesn't exist" || fail "tls-ask said yes to an unknown shop: ${unknown:0:120}"
if [ -n "$SHOP" ]; then
  SB="https://$SHOP.$APP_DOMAIN"
  page="$("${CURL[@]}" "$SB/" 2>&1)"
  echo "$page" | grep -q 'name="lw-shop"' && pass "$SB opens over HTTPS with its lw-shop marker" || fail "$SB: no lw-shop marker"
  bad=""
  for p in /api/health /internal/tls-ask /build /r/x /assets/x.js; do
    code="$("${CURL[@]}" -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$SB$p")"; [ "$code" = "404" ] || bad="$bad $p=$code"
  done
  [ -z "$bad" ] && pass "shop host serves no app paths (/api /internal /build /r /assets: 404)" || fail "shop host answered:$bad"
else
  info "(no live real shop yet: shop-host checks skipped)"
fi

echo "4. Accounts"
admin="$(inapp <<'PY' 2>&1
from sqlmodel import Session, select
from app.config import get_settings
from app.db import get_engine
from app.models import User
s = get_settings()
with Session(get_engine()) as db:
    u = db.exec(select(User).where(User.email == s.admin_email.strip().lower())).first() if s.admin_email else None
    print("ADMIN", "unset" if not s.admin_email else ("ok" if u and u.role == "admin" and u.status == "approved" else "missing"))
    print("DEVMODE", s.dev_mode)
    print("MAILBOX", s.mailbox_expires_on or "unset")
PY
)"
case "$(echo "$admin" | awk '/^ADMIN/{print $2}')" in
  ok) pass "the ADMIN_EMAIL user exists, approved, role admin";;
  unset) fail "ADMIN_EMAIL is not set";;
  *) fail "the ADMIN_EMAIL user is missing or not admin";;
esac
[ "$(echo "$admin" | awk '/^DEVMODE/{print $2}')" = "False" ] && pass "DEV_MODE is off" || fail "DEV_MODE is on"
mb="$(echo "$admin" | awk '/^MAILBOX/{print $2}')"
if [ "$mb" = "unset" ]; then $LOCAL && info "MAILBOX_EXPIRES_ON unset (fine locally)" || fail "MAILBOX_EXPIRES_ON is not set (health can't warn before hello@ lapses)"
else pass "MAILBOX_EXPIRES_ON = $mb (health warns 14 days ahead)"; fi
# A one-time sign-in token for the admin, made inside the app and used once over https, then signed out.

from sqlmodel import Session

PY

if [ -n "$TOKEN" ]; then
  hdrs="$(mktemp)"

  flags="$(echo "$cookie" | sed -E 's/^set-cookie: __Host-lw_session=[^;]*//I')"  # the value is never shown

  raw="$(echo "$cookie" | sed -E 's/^set-cookie: __Host-lw_session=([^;]*).*/\1/I')"

echo "5. One app process"
procs="$(inapp <<'PY' 2>&1
import os

PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# M1 acceptance check. Run ON THE VPS, from the repo, with the stack running:
#
#   bash scripts/check_m1.sh
#   EXTERNAL_SUBJECT="hello from my gmail" bash scripts/check_m1.sh   # also look for your external test email
#
# Prints PASS / FAIL for each M1 criterion (docs/BUILD_PLAN.md):
#   1. https://<APP_DOMAIN> loads with a valid certificate (+ DNS: app domain and wildcard point here)
#   2. the mailbox is reachable (SMTP + IMAP login with the .env password, inside the app container)
#      and, if EXTERNAL_SUBJECT is set, the external test email is in the inbox
#   3. a contact-form submission arrives in the mailbox (found over IMAP by a unique marker)
#   4. the SMTP password is only in the server .env: not tracked, not in any file or commit
# Secrets are never printed. Exit code = number of failures.

set -uo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO"
FAILS=0
pass() { printf '  \033[32mPASS\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() { printf '  \033[31mFAIL\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); }
info() { printf '        %s\n' "$1"; }

# Read one value from .env without printing it (no `source`: values may contain spaces/symbols).
envval() { grep -E "^$1=" .env 2>/dev/null | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2- | sed -e 's/[[:space:]]#.*$//' -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//' -e "s/^'//" -e "s/'$//"; }

if [ ! -f .env ]; then
  echo "FAIL: no .env in $REPO (see docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md step 5)"; exit 1
fi
APP_DOMAIN="$(envval APP_DOMAIN)"
SERVER_IP="$(envval SERVER_IP)"
COMPOSE=(docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml)
echo "M1 check for https://$APP_DOMAIN (server $SERVER_IP)"

# ---------- 1. HTTPS + DNS ----------
echo "1. Website over HTTPS"
if [ -z "$APP_DOMAIN" ] || [ "$APP_DOMAIN" = "localhost" ]; then
  fail "APP_DOMAIN is not set to your real domain in .env"
else
  for host in "$APP_DOMAIN" "m1-check-$RANDOM.$APP_DOMAIN"; do
    ip="$(getent ahostsv4 "$host" | awk 'NR==1{print $1}')"
    label="$host"; [ "$host" != "$APP_DOMAIN" ] && label="wildcard *.$APP_DOMAIN"
    if [ -n "$ip" ] && [ "$ip" = "$SERVER_IP" ]; then pass "DNS: $label -> $ip"
    else fail "DNS: $label -> ${ip:-nothing} (want $SERVER_IP; DNS can take up to an hour)"; fi
  done
  if body="$(curl -sS --max-time 15 "https://$APP_DOMAIN/api/health" 2>&1)" && echo "$body" | grep -q '"ok":true'; then
    pass "https://$APP_DOMAIN loads with a valid certificate"
    end="$(echo | openssl s_client -connect "$APP_DOMAIN:443" -servername "$APP_DOMAIN" 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -enddate 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2)"
    [ -n "$end" ] && info "certificate valid until $end"
  else
    fail "https://$APP_DOMAIN/api/health: ${body:0:200}"
  fi
  code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 "https://$APP_DOMAIN/internal/tls-ask?domain=x")"
  [ "$code" = "404" ] && pass "/internal/* is not reachable from outside" || fail "/internal/* answered $code (want 404)"
fi

# Run Python inside the app container (it has the .env values; nothing is printed but results).
inapp() { "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T app python - "$@"; }

if [ -z "$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q app 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  fail "the app container isn't running (docker compose ... up -d)"; echo "$FAILS failure(s)"; exit "$FAILS"
fi

# ---------- 2. Mailbox reachable ----------
echo "2. Mailbox"
out="$(inapp "${EXTERNAL_SUBJECT:-}" <<'PY' 2>&1
import imaplib, os, smtplib, ssl, sys
user = os.environ.get("SMTP_USER", "")
ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
try:
    with smtplib.SMTP_SSL(os.environ.get("SMTP_HOST", "smtpout.secureserver.net"), int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", 465)), context=ctx, timeout=20) as s:
        s.login(user, os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD", ""))
    print("SMTP_OK", user)
except Exception as e:
    print("SMTP_FAIL", type(e).__name__, str(e)[:120].replace(os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD", "") or "\0", "***"))
try:
    m = imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(os.environ.get("IMAP_HOST", "imap.secureserver.net"), int(os.environ.get("IMAP_PORT", 993)), ssl_context=ctx)
    m.login(os.environ.get("IMAP_USER", ""), os.environ.get("IMAP_PASSWORD", ""))
    m.select("INBOX", readonly=True)
    print("IMAP_OK")
    subj = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ""
    if subj:
        typ, data = m.search(None, "SUBJECT", '"%s"' % subj.replace('"', ""))
        print("EXTERNAL_FOUND" if data and data[0].split() else "EXTERNAL_MISSING")
    m.logout()
except Exception as e:
    print("IMAP_FAIL", type(e).__name__, str(e)[:120])
PY
)"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^SMTP_OK' && pass "SMTP login as $(echo "$out" | awk '/^SMTP_OK/{print $2}') (smtpout.secureserver.net:465)" \
  || fail "SMTP login: $(echo "$out" | grep '^SMTP_FAIL' | cut -d' ' -f2-)"
echo "$out" | grep -q '^IMAP_OK' && pass "IMAP login (inbox readable)" || fail "IMAP login: $(echo "$out" | grep '^IMAP_FAIL' | cut -d' ' -f2-)"
if [ -n "${EXTERNAL_SUBJECT:-}" ]; then
  echo "$out" | grep -q '^EXTERNAL_FOUND' && pass "external test email \"$EXTERNAL_SUBJECT\" is in the inbox" \
    || fail "external test email \"$EXTERNAL_SUBJECT\" not found in the inbox"
else
  info "(manual) send an email from another account, then re-run with EXTERNAL_SUBJECT=\"<its subject>\""
fi

# ---------- 3. Contact form arrives ----------
echo "3. Contact form"
MARK="m1check-$(date +%s)-$RANDOM"
resp="$(curl -sS --max-time 20 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"name\":\"M1 check\",\"email\":\"m1-check@example.org\",\"message\":\"Automatic M1 check $MARK\"}" \
  "https://$APP_DOMAIN/api/contact" 2>&1)"
if echo "$resp" | grep -q '"ok":true'; then
  pass "contact form accepted the message"
  found="$(inapp "$MARK" <<'PY' 2>&1
import imaplib, os, ssl, sys, time
mark = sys.argv[1]
for _ in range(12):  # up to ~2 minutes
    try:
        m = imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(os.environ.get("IMAP_HOST", "imap.secureserver.net"), int(os.environ.get("IMAP_PORT", 993)), ssl_context=ssl.create_default_context())
        m.login(os.environ.get("IMAP_USER", ""), os.environ.get("IMAP_PASSWORD", ""))
        m.select("INBOX", readonly=True)
        typ, data = m.search(None, "BODY", '"%s"' % mark)
        m.logout()
        if data and data[0].split():
            print("FOUND"); sys.exit(0)
    except Exception as e:
        print("ERR", type(e).__name__)
    time.sleep(10)
print("MISSING")
PY
)"
  echo "$found" | grep -q '^FOUND' && pass "contact form message arrived in the mailbox" \
    || fail "contact form message not in the inbox after 2 minutes ($(echo "$found" | tail -n1))"
else
  fail "contact form: ${resp:0:200}"
fi

# ---------- 4. Password only in server .env ----------
echo "4. Secrets"
git ls-files --error-unmatch .env >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail ".env is tracked by git!" || pass ".env is not tracked by git"
PW="$(envval SMTP_PASSWORD)"
if [ -z "$PW" ]; then
  fail "SMTP_PASSWORD is empty in .env"
else
  # -f <(...) keeps the password off every command line (ps can't see it).
  if git grep -qF -f <(printf '%s\n' "$PW") -- . 2>/dev/null; then fail "SMTP password found in a tracked file (git grep)"
  else pass "git grep: SMTP password not in any tracked file"; fi
  if git log -p --all 2>/dev/null | grep -qF -f <(printf '%s\n' "$PW"); then fail "SMTP password found in git history"
  else pass "SMTP password not in any commit"; fi
fi
unset PW

echo
if [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]; then echo "M1: all checks passed."; else echo "M1: $FAILS check(s) failed."; fi
exit "$FAILS"

# deploy/

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `Dockerfile` | One image: React build baked in, FastAPI + seller sites, `/build` replay page. Runs as `lw` (uid 10001), **one uvicorn worker**, healthcheck on `/api/health`. No dev dependencies (`requirements.txt` only). |
| `docker-compose.yml` | Base: `app` (port 8000 **not published**) + `caddy` (the only service with ports: 80/443). Volumes: `app-data` (SQLite), `caddy-data` (certificates). |
| `docker-compose.prod.yml` | On top of the base, on the VPS: `Caddyfile.prod`, monitoring on, `restart: unless-stopped`, healthchecks, capped logs. |
| `docker-compose.local.yml` | On top of base + prod, on your computer: the **production-like local stack** (below). |
| `Caddyfile.prod` | HTTPS for the app (HSTS), on-demand TLS for shops (`ask` → `/internal/tls-ask`), `/internal/*` → 404 on every host, 8 MB body limit, timeouts. Used both on the VPS and locally. |
| `Caddyfile` | Quick plain-http mode (`docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up`): signing in needs `DEV_MODE=true` there. |

There's no uploads volume because nothing uploaded is stored. Price-list photos are read in memory and sent to the
Reader (`routers/businesses.py`). The state is the SQLite file on `app-data` plus Caddy's certificates on `caddy-data`.
`.env` lives only on the server (`chmod 600`). It's excluded from the image by `.dockerignore`, and the local
stack doesn't read it.

## The production-like local stack

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml up -d --build --wait
bash scripts/check_m1.sh --local          # the same checks as on the VPS
cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npx playwright test   # browser flows over https
```

- App: https://launchwitness.localhost · shops: `https://<slug>.launchwitness.localhost` (`*.localhost` is always
  this computer). Caddy issues certificates from its **own local CA** (`local_certs`), including on-demand ones for
  shops after `tls-ask` says yes. The browser tests accept that CA (`ignoreHTTPSErrors`, only for `.localhost`).
  `check_m1.sh --local` copies the CA's root out of the Caddy container and verifies against it.
- `DEV_MODE=false` (real `__Host-` cookies), `USE_FAKES=true` (pretend GoDaddy, DNS and inbox), `CLAUDE_MODE=fixture`.
- **Every email goes to Mailpit** (http://localhost:8025; sign-in links arrive there). `SMTP_SECURITY=plain` is
  allowed only for a one-word docker host such as `mailpit` (the settings refuse it for any real host name).
- It **never reads `../.env`** (`env_file: !reset []`), so no real key gets into a local container.
- Admin: sign in as `admin@launchwitness.localhost` (the link arrives in Mailpit).
- Restart drill: `PRACTICE_STEP_SECONDS=3 docker compose ... up -d`, then `scripts/restart_drill.py` (see its header)
  starts a practice launch you can kill with `docker compose ... kill -s KILL app`.
- Stop: `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml down`
  (add `-v` to forget the local database and CA).

## Rules that keep it safe (don't "improve" these)

- **One app container, one worker.** APScheduler runs in-process and SQLite has one writer. The app takes a lock
  next to the database at startup and refuses to start a second process (`app/singleton.py`), and it also refuses
  `WEB_CONCURRENCY` > 1. Never add `--workers`, never `--scale app=2`.
- **Only Caddy publishes ports.** The rate limits read the last `X-Forwarded-For` entry, which Caddy always sets
  to the real client and which a client can't forge (no `trusted_proxies`). If port 8000 were ever published,
  anyone could pick their own rate-limit identity.
- **`/internal/*` is closed twice:** Caddy answers 404 on every host, and the app itself answers only to private
  host names (`app:8000`, an IP, a one-word name), never to `launchwitness.com` or a shop.

| # | Mismatch | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The local Caddyfile is plain http, so `__Host-` cookies (`DEV_MODE=false`) can't work through Docker. The production cookie path couldn't be tested before the VPS. | `docker-compose.local.yml` runs `Caddyfile.prod` with Caddy's local CA. |
| 2 | Sign-in emails always go through real SMTP. A local `DEV_MODE=false` run would have used GoDaddy SMTP with the real password from `.env`. | Mailpit catch-all + `SMTP_SECURITY=plain` (one-word hosts only). |
| 3 | The base compose loads `../.env` into the container for local runs too, putting real secrets in a local container. | The local override resets `env_file`. |
| 4 | `Caddyfile.prod` had no HSTS, no timeouts, no body-size limit, and sent the `Server` header. `/internal` (no slash) wasn't matched. | Added all; the matcher is `/internal /internal/*`. |
| 5 | Nothing stopped `--workers 4` (4 copies of every alert and daily test order). | `--workers 1` pinned and commented, plus the startup lock and the `WEB_CONCURRENCY` check. |
| 6 | `--forwarded-allow-ips *` makes `request.client` the *leftmost* XFF entry. That's safe only because Caddy overwrites XFF and `visitor_id` reads the last entry. | Documented (Dockerfile + here). Proven: forged XFF doesn't dodge the limit. |
| 7 | `/internal/*` was blocked only by Caddy; the app answered it on any Host. | The request guard refuses `/internal` for any dotted host name. |
| 8 | `check_m1.sh` checked a **wildcard** record (dropped in S9F), had no cookie / shop-host / one-process / admin checks, and ran only on the VPS. | Rewritten. Same checks `--local` and on the VPS. |
| 9 | RUNBOOK step 4 said to add `*`; step 8 said Titan; step 10 said to paste `ADMIN_TOKEN` into `#/admin`. SPEC, BUILD_PLAN and PROGRESS also said wildcard. | Updated. The VPS steps are now `docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md`. |
| 10 | `backup_db.sh` kept 14 copies with no weekly ones. Its restore copied over the live DB **without removing `-wal`/`-shm`** (an old WAL could be replayed into the restored file), and the restore was never tested. | Part B: online backup, 7 daily + 4 weekly, `restore_db.sh`, tested. |
| 11 | SQLite had no WAL, `busy_timeout` or `foreign_keys`. | Set on every connection. Turning on foreign keys exposed a real bug (the admin demo delete left proof rows behind); fixed. |
| 12 | The prod compose said `restart: always`. | `unless-stopped`. |
| 13 | The data directory was mode 755. | 700, owned by `lw`. |
| 14 | `HEAD /` answers 405 (FastAPI GET routes don't take HEAD). Browsers don't care; an uptime monitor that uses HEAD would. | **Not fixed**: point any monitor at `GET /api/health`. |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Back up the app's SQLite database from the running `app` container with SQLite's ONLINE backup API
# (consistent while the app runs; never a `cp` of a live WAL database), check it, and rotate:
# 7 daily copies in backups/daily/ plus 4 weekly copies in backups/weekly/ (one a week).
#
#   bash scripts/backup_db.sh [backup-dir]          # default <repo>/backups (git-ignored), mode 600 files
#   LOCAL=1 bash scripts/backup_db.sh               # the local production-like stack (deploy/README.md)
# Restore: bash scripts/restore_db.sh <backup file>
# Nightly on the VPS (crontab -e), 03:15 server time:
#   15 3 * * * cd $HOME/LaunchWitness && bash scripts/backup_db.sh >> backups/backup.log 2>&1
#
# OFF-SERVER COPY: not automated (no cloud service chosen). The owner copies backups/ off the VPS by hand, e.g.
#   scp -i ~/.ssh/launchwitness -r lw@<VPS_IP>:LaunchWitness/backups ./lw-backups-$(date +%F)
# A backup that only lives on the server is lost with the server.

set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
DIR="${1:-$REPO/backups}"
KEEP_DAILY="${KEEP_DAILY:-7}"
KEEP_WEEKLY="${KEEP_WEEKLY:-4}"
if [ "${LOCAL:-}" = "1" ]; then
  COMPOSE=(docker compose -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.yml" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.local.yml")
else
  ENV_ARGS=()
  [ -f "$REPO/.env" ] && ENV_ARGS=(--env-file "$REPO/.env")
  COMPOSE=(docker compose "${ENV_ARGS[@]}" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.yml" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml")
fi

CID="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q app)"
[ -n "$CID" ] || { echo "FAIL: the app container isn't running." >&2; exit 1; }

umask 077
mkdir -p "$DIR/daily" "$DIR/weekly"
TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
TMP="/app/backend/data/.backup-$TS.db"
OUT="$DIR/daily/launchwitness-$TS.db"

COUNTS="$(docker exec -i "$CID" python -m app.backup create "$TMP")"
docker cp "$CID:$TMP" "$OUT" >/dev/null
docker exec "$CID" rm -f "$TMP"
chmod 600 "$OUT"

# One weekly copy when the newest weekly one is 7+ days old (or there is none).
if [ -z "$(find "$DIR/weekly" -name 'launchwitness-*.db' -mtime -7 2>/dev/null | head -n1)" ]; then
  cp -p "$OUT" "$DIR/weekly/"
  echo "weekly copy: $DIR/weekly/$(basename "$OUT")"
fi
ls -1t "$DIR"/daily/launchwitness-*.db 2>/dev/null | tail -n +"$((KEEP_DAILY + 1))" | xargs -r rm -f
ls -1t "$DIR"/weekly/launchwitness-*.db 2>/dev/null | tail -n +"$((KEEP_WEEKLY + 1))" | xargs -r rm -f

echo "OK: $OUT ($(du -h "$OUT" | cut -f1)); rows $COUNTS"
echo "Kept: $(ls "$DIR"/daily/*.db | wc -l) daily, $(ls "$DIR"/weekly/*.db 2>/dev/null | wc -l) weekly."
echo "Restore (stops the app briefly): bash scripts/restore_db.sh $OUT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Restore the app's database from a backup made by scripts/backup_db.sh.
#
#   bash scripts/restore_db.sh backups/daily/launchwitness-<time>.db
#   LOCAL=1 bash scripts/restore_db.sh <file>      # the local production-like stack
#
# What it does: (1) a safety backup of the CURRENT database first (backups/pre-restore-<time>.db), (2) stops the
# app (Caddy keeps running and shows an error page for a moment), (3) checks the backup, deletes the old -wal/-shm
# files and copies the backup in with SQLite's backup API (app/backup.py, as the app user), (4) compares row counts
# with the backup, (5) starts the app and waits until it's healthy.

set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="${1:?usage: bash scripts/restore_db.sh <backup file>}"
[ -f "$SRC" ] || { echo "FAIL: no such file: $SRC" >&2; exit 1; }
SRC="$(cd "$(dirname "$SRC")" && pwd)/$(basename "$SRC")"
if [ "${LOCAL:-}" = "1" ]; then
  COMPOSE=(docker compose -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.yml" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.local.yml")
else
  ENV_ARGS=()
  [ -f "$REPO/.env" ] && ENV_ARGS=(--env-file "$REPO/.env")
  COMPOSE=(docker compose "${ENV_ARGS[@]}" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.yml" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml")
fi

umask 077
mkdir -p "$REPO/backups"
if [ -n "$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q app)" ]; then
  CID="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q app)"
  TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
  docker exec -i "$CID" python -m app.backup create "/app/backend/data/.pre-restore-$TS.db" >/dev/null
  docker cp "$CID:/app/backend/data/.pre-restore-$TS.db" "$REPO/backups/pre-restore-$TS.db" >/dev/null
  docker exec "$CID" rm -f "/app/backend/data/.pre-restore-$TS.db"
  echo "safety copy of the current database: backups/pre-restore-$TS.db"
fi

WANT="$(cd "$REPO/backend" 2>/dev/null && python3 -c "import sqlite3,json,sys
con=sqlite3.connect('file:'+sys.argv[1]+'?mode=ro',uri=True)
n=[r[0] for r in con.execute(\"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%'\")]
print(json.dumps({t:con.execute(f'SELECT count(*) FROM \"{t}\"').fetchone()[0] for t in sorted(n)}))" "$SRC" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"

"${COMPOSE[@]}" stop app
# The app image, with the backup mounted read-only, running as the app user (it owns the data volume).
GOT="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" run --rm --no-deps -T -v "$SRC:/restore.db:ro" --entrypoint python app -m app.backup restore /restore.db)"
"${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d --wait app >/dev/null
echo "restored rows: $GOT"
if [ -n "$WANT" ] && [ "$WANT" != "$GOT" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: row counts differ from the backup file: $WANT" >&2; exit 1
fi
echo "OK: restored $SRC and the app is healthy again."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Back up the app's SQLite database from the running `app` container with SQLite's ONLINE backup API
# (consistent while the app runs; never a `cp` of a live WAL database), check it, and rotate:

#
#   bash scripts/backup_db.sh [backup-dir]          # default <repo>/backups (git-ignored), mode 600 files
#   LOCAL=1 bash scripts/backup_db.sh               # the local production-like stack (deploy/README.md)
# Restore: bash scripts/restore_db.sh <backup file>

#
# OFF-SERVER COPY: not automated (no cloud service chosen). The owner copies backups/ off the VPS by hand, e.g.
#   scp -i ~/.ssh/launchwitness -r lw@<VPS_IP>:LaunchWitness/backups ./lw-backups-$(date +%F)
# A backup that only lives on the server is lost with the server.

set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
DIR="${1:-$REPO/backups}"
KEEP_DAILY="${KEEP_DAILY:-7}"
KEEP_WEEKLY="${KEEP_WEEKLY:-4}"

mkdir -p "$DIR/daily" "$DIR/weekly"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Back up the app's SQLite database from the running `app` container (safe while the app runs:
# uses SQLite's online backup API), keep the newest $KEEP copies, and print how to restore.
#
# Usage (on the VPS, from anywhere):   bash scripts/backup_db.sh [backup-dir]
#   default backup-dir: <repo>/backups (git-ignored).  KEEP=14 by default.
# Restore:  bash scripts/backup_db.sh --restore backups/launchwitness-<time>.db
#   (stops the app, copies the file onto the data volume owned by the app user, starts the app)
# Nightly (crontab -e):   15 3 * * * cd ~/LaunchWitness && bash scripts/backup_db.sh >> backups/backup.log 2>&1

set -euo pipefail

REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
DIR="${1:-$REPO/backups}"
KEEP="${KEEP:-14}"
ENV_ARGS=()
[ -f "$REPO/.env" ] && ENV_ARGS=(--env-file "$REPO/.env")
COMPOSE=(docker compose "${ENV_ARGS[@]}" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.yml" -f "$REPO/deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml")

if [ "${1:-}" = "--restore" ]; then
  FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "${2:?backup file to restore}")" && pwd)/$(basename "$2")"
  [ -f "$FILE" ] || { echo "FAIL: no such file: $FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" stop app
  # Run the app image as root just to copy the file and hand it to the app user (uid lw).
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" run --rm --no-deps --user root -v "$FILE:/restore.db:ro" --entrypoint sh app -c \
    'cp /restore.db /app/backend/data/launchwitness.db && chown lw /app/backend/data/launchwitness.db && chmod 600 /app/backend/data/launchwitness.db'
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" start app
  echo "OK: restored $FILE. Check: curl -s https://\$APP_DOMAIN/api/health"
  exit 0
fi

CID="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q app)"
if [ -z "$CID" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: the app container isn't running. Start it first (see docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md)." >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$DIR"
TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
TMP="/app/backend/data/.backup-$TS.db"
OUT="$DIR/launchwitness-$TS.db"

# Online backup inside the container, to the data volume.
docker exec -i "$CID" python - "$TMP" <<'PY'
import sqlite3, sys
from app.config import get_settings
url = get_settings().database_url
assert url.startswith("sqlite:///"), f"not a SQLite file database: {url}"
src = sqlite3.connect(url.removeprefix("sqlite:///"))
dst = sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[1])
src.backup(dst)
ok = dst.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0]
dst.close(); src.close()
assert ok == "ok", ok
PY
docker cp "$CID:$TMP" "$OUT" >/dev/null
docker exec "$CID" rm -f "$TMP"
chmod 600 "$OUT"   # holds customer names/phones: owner-only

# Keep the newest $KEEP backups.
ls -1t "$DIR"/launchwitness-*.db 2>/dev/null | tail -n +"$((KEEP + 1))" | xargs -r rm -f

echo "OK: backed up to $OUT ($(du -h "$OUT" | cut -f1)), keeping the newest $KEEP."
echo "Restore (stops the app briefly):  bash scripts/backup_db.sh --restore $OUT"

def _db_with_rows(path, n):
    engine = make_engine(f"sqlite:///{path}")
    init_db(engine)
    with Session(engine) as s:
        for i in range(n):
            s.add(Business(name=f"Shop {i}", subdomain=f"shop-{i}"))

def test_backup_then_restore_gives_back_the_same_rows(tmp_path):
    from app import backup

    live = tmp_path / "live.db"
    engine = _db_with_rows(live, 3)
    with engine.connect() as c:  # the app is "running": an open WAL connection with recent writes
        c.exec_driver_sql("SELECT 1")
        snap = backup.create(str(live), str(tmp_path / "b.db"))
        assert snap["business"] == 3
    with Session(engine) as s:  # life goes on after the backup
        s.add(Business(name="After", subdomain="after"))
        s.commit()
    engine.dispose()
    assert backup.counts(str(live))["business"] == 4
    assert (tmp_path / "live.db-wal").exists() or True
    restored = backup.restore(str(tmp_path / "b.db"), str(live))
    assert restored == snap and restored["business"] == 3
    assert not (tmp_path / "live.db-wal").exists()  # an old WAL never survives a restore
    names = [b.name for b in Session(make_engine(f"sqlite:///{live}")).exec(select(Business)).all()]
    assert names == ["Shop 0", "Shop 1", "Shop 2"]

Privacy

What we keep about you, and why

LaunchWitness is a small beta service. This page lists everything we store, in plain words. It is not legal advice, and we'll update it as the service changes.

What we store

  • Your email address: to sign you in (we email you a link; there are no passwords) and to send you your shop's orders and warnings.
  • Your shop: what you typed or photographed (description, price list), the website made from it, its address, and the checks we run on it (what we saw, and when).
  • Your customers' orders: the name and phone number a customer types, what they ordered, and their note. These are kept so you can see and export your orders.
  • Records of what happened (an audit log): sign-ins, launches, changes and checks, with the time. We keep these to find mistakes and abuse.
  • For limits and safety only: a one-way scrambled form of your internet address (never the address itself) and your browser's name, so we can stop one person from using up everyone's limits.

We don't sell any of it, we don't show ads, and we don't use tracking or advertising cookies.

Cookies

Two cookies, both only for this site: one keeps you signed in (14 days), and one keeps a practice shop you made without signing in (1 day). Shop pages never receive them.

Who else sees some of it

  • Anthropic (Claude) reads your description and price list (or photo) to write your website, and checks a new shop against our rules before it goes live.
  • GoDaddy hosts our server, our email and the address records of live shops.
  • Let's Encrypt issues each live shop's security certificate. Certificates are recorded in public logs, so a live shop's address becomes public.

How long we keep it

  • A practice shop made without signing in: deleted after 24 hours.
  • Your shops and their orders: until you delete the shop or your account.
  • Sign-in links work once, for 15 minutes; only a scrambled form of them is stored.
  • Backups of the database are kept for up to 4 weeks, then overwritten. Something you delete can stay in a backup until then.

Deleting everything

Go to Your account → Delete my account. We email you a link to confirm. That removes your account, your shops, their orders and their records; we keep one line saying an account was deleted, without your details. You can also delete a single shop on its page, or write to us.

); } export function TermsPage() { return (

Terms of use

The deal, in plain words

By using LaunchWitness you agree to these terms. They're written simply on purpose. They're not legal advice.

What LaunchWitness does

It builds a simple website for your home business from what you describe, puts it at an address under launchwitness.com, checks that a test order really reaches you, and keeps checking. It's a beta: things can break, and we may change or stop the service. We'll tell you by email before we stop it.

Your part

  • Only describe a business that is yours, and only sell things that are legal where you are.
  • No medicines, weapons, adult content, gambling, alcohol or tobacco, no copies of other brands, and nothing that misleads customers. Our team may pause or remove a shop that breaks this, and tell you why.
  • Check your website's details and prices. You're responsible for your products, prices and orders.
  • Keep your email account safe: whoever can read it can sign in as you.

Money

LaunchWitness takes no payments and never buys anything for you automatically. Customers pay you directly. If something needs money (like renewing a website name), we tell you, and you decide.

Our part, and its limits

We work to keep your shop online and to tell you when something breaks. We can't promise it will always be up, or that every order will arrive. Please don't rely on it as your only way to take orders yet. As far as the law allows, we aren't responsible for lost orders or lost sales.

Ending

You can delete your account at any time (Your account). We may suspend an account that breaks these terms or puts others at risk. See the Privacy page for what happens to your data.

); } export function LegalLinks() { return ( Privacy · Terms ); }

@router.post("/account/delete")
def delete_account(body: Confirm, response: Response, user: Annotated[User, Depends(require_user)],
                   settings: Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)],
                   session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)],
                   server: Annotated[Integrations, Depends(get_integrations)],
                   practice: Annotated[Integrations, Depends(get_practice_integrations)]) -> dict:
    """Unpublish and delete the user's shops, remove memberships and personal data, end every
    session, and keep one anonymous audit record. Needs the emailed link AND being signed in."""
    row = accounts.consume_token(session, body.token, "delete_account", email=user.email)
    if row is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=EXPIRED)
    if user.role == "admin":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="The admin account can't be deleted here.")
    shops = session.exec(select(Business).join(Membership, Membership.business_id == Business.id)
                         .where(Membership.user_id == user.id, Membership.role == "owner")).all()
    for b in shops:
        purge_business(session, settings, for_business(b, server, practice), b)
    user_id = user.id
    accounts.revoke_sessions(session, user_id)
    user.email, user.status, user.status_reason = f"deleted-{user_id}@deleted.invalid", "deleted", ""
    session.add(user)
    session.commit()
    audit.record(session, actor="owner", action="account_deleted", target=f"user:{user_id}", result="ok",
                 detail=f"{len(shops)} shop(s) removed; email erased")  # no email, no shop names
    accounts.clear_cookie(response, settings, settings.session_cookie)
    return {"ok": True}

What we keep about you, and why

LaunchWitness is a small beta service. This page lists everything we store, in plain words. It is not legal advice, and we'll update it as the service changes.

## 8. Architecture and GoDaddy usage

One GoDaddy Docker VPS (4 vCPU / 8 GB, provided at $0) runs everything; GoDaddy and Claude are called as APIs.

- **Caddy:** HTTPS for the app and every seller site; on-demand TLS with an `ask` endpoint that only approves domains in the DB.
- **FastAPI:** agents, API, monitoring scheduler, and every seller site (served by `Host` header from one template + profile).
- **React (Vite):** seller-facing app, built and served as static files.
- **SQLite:** profiles, plans, DNS backups, check results, audit log.
- **Outside:** Claude API; GoDaddy Domains/DNS/Email (OTE sandbox in dev, `GODADDY_ENV=ote|prod`); SMTP through the app's one mailbox.
- **Secrets** live only in environment variables.
- **Sandbox subdomains** get one A record each (`<slug>.<APP_DOMAIN>` → VPS), written by the app at launch; no wildcard (decided S9F). Only `@` (and optionally `www`) is made by hand.

| Step | GoDaddy piece | Calls |
|---|---|---|
| Name | Domains API (or `gddy`) | availability, suggestions, price quote |
| Buy | godaddy.com checkout with credit (demo); Domains API purchase only behind guards | purchase after approval |
| Point | DNS API | list records (backup), set A, MX, SPF/DKIM/DMARC |
| Mailbox | Titan email via `gddy` / Email API | create mailbox, poll until ready |
| Host | Docker VPS | A record → VPS; Caddy issues HTTPS |
| Undo | DNS API | write backup back |

**Access limits:** production Availability API needs 50+ domains or ~$20/month spend; DNS API needs ≥1 domain. So: buy the app domain first; check availability via `gddy`, OTE, or free RDAP if production stays blocked.

Say plainly to judges: hosting is the Docker VPS, not GoDaddy's Hosting API.

---

## 9. Safety rules

1. **Approve before spending.** Purchase/mailbox only after Approve on a card showing exact cost.
2. **Preview before changing.** Every DNS change shown as a before/after diff first.
3. **Back up, then undo.** Before any DNS write, save current records as JSON. Failed launch check can write the backup back. Failed mailbox step is retried, not undone.
4. **Scoped actions.** Each launch touches only its own domain. Doctor picks from a fixed playbook; anything else is refused and logged.
5. **Spend guards in code.** `ALLOW_PURCHASE=false` default, hard `MAX_SPEND_USD` cap, purchase only when flag on AND owner approved.

Every step goes to the audit log shown in the report.

---

## 9a. Accounts and tenancy (session 9F)

- **Guest practice.** "Try it" needs no account: an anonymous cookie owns a practice workspace (pretend GoDaddy, never public, deleted after 24 hours).
- **Sign in by emailed link.** No passwords. The link carries 32 random bytes, only its SHA-256 is stored, it works once for 15 minutes, and only the "Sign in" button (a POST) uses it, so mail scanners opening the link change nothing. Same answer whether or not the address has an account. Limits per address and per IP. Signing in keeps the guest's shops (up to the limit). There is no other "claim" mechanism.
- **Sessions.** `__Host-lw_session`: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain (host-only), so shop subdomains never receive it. New id at every sign-in; 14-day sliding expiry; log out; log out everywhere; suspension ends every session at once. CSRF: Origin check + a token derived from the cookie on every change.
- **Tenancy.** Every business route goes through one gate; the ownership filter is part of the database query; another owner's shop answers 404. Shoppers never sign in.
- **Team approval during the beta.** New accounts are *pending* (practice only) until the team approves them. The admin is the `ADMIN_EMAIL` user; `ADMIN_TOKEN` stays for the command line only.
- **Limits.** 3 shops per account; a daily cap on describes (Claude calls) that deleting shops doesn't reset; **at most `MAX_LIVE_SHOPS` (40) live shops**, because Let's Encrypt issues about 50 new certificates per registered domain per week and every shop subdomain needs its own.
- **Orders and alerts** go to the owners' verified sign-in addresses (the app mailbox only for shops the team runs, or ownerless guest shops).
- **Go-live gate.** At real approval: approved account, not a guest shop, not paused, under the live-shop cap, policy check OK (or cleared by the team).
- **Deleting an account** needs the emailed link *and* being signed in; it unpublishes and deletes the shops, erases the email and keeps one anonymous audit row.
- Route classes live in `backend/app/safety/route_table.py`; a test fails on any unclassified route.

---

## 10. Budget
77:Out of scope: payment gateways or holding money (UPI pay links only; "Connect Razorpay (after seller KYC)" is future work), appointments/booking, inventory, SMS, WhatsApp Business / Instagram APIs, multiple templates, custom code generation.

def days_left(when: datetime | None) -> int | None:
    if when is None:
        return None
    if when.tzinfo is None:
        when = when.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
    return (when - datetime.now(UTC)).days


def expiry_info(ctx: Ctx) -> dict:
    info: dict = {"cert_days_left": None, "domain_days_left": None}
    try:
        info["cert_days_left"] = days_left(ctx.integ.http.cert_expires(ctx.plan.site_host))
        if ctx.plan.mode == "full":  # sandbox addresses live under the app's own domain
            info["domain_days_left"] = days_left(ctx.integ.godaddy.domain_expires(ctx.plan.zone))
    except Exception as e:  # informational only; never breaks a check run
        info["error"] = type(e).__name__
    return info

def report(b: Annotated[Business, Depends(require_business_access)], actor: ActorDep,
           settings: Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)],
           session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)],
           integ_for: Annotated[IntegFor, Depends(integrations_for)]) -> dict:
    admin = actor.is_admin
    practice = b.practice or integ_for(b).fake  # results from the pretend world are always labelled
    plan = latest_launched_plan(session, b.id)
    latest_plan = session.exec(select(Plan).where(Plan.business_id == b.id, Plan.practice == b.practice)
                               .order_by(Plan.id.desc())).first()
    run_row = session.exec(select(CheckRun).where(CheckRun.business_id == b.id, CheckRun.trigger.in_(OWNER_RUNS))
                           .order_by(CheckRun.id.desc())).first()
    run = run_out(session, run_row) if run_row and plan else None
    proven = proof.summary(session, run)  # adds each check's hops + state ("proven" / "needs_you" / "failed")
    ready, title, left = headline(plan, latest_plan, run, practice)

    def last(trigger: str) -> dict | None:
        r = session.exec(select(CheckRun).where(CheckRun.business_id == b.id, CheckRun.trigger == trigger,
                                                CheckRun.status == "done").order_by(CheckRun.id.desc())).first()
        return {"at": iso(r.finished_at), "passed": r.passed} if r else None

    info_row = session.exec(select(CheckRun).where(CheckRun.business_id == b.id, CheckRun.status == "done")
                            .order_by(CheckRun.id.desc())).first()
    info = json.loads(info_row.info_json) if info_row else {}
    events = session.exec(select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.business_id == b.id)
                          .order_by(AuditEvent.id.desc()).limit(AUDIT_LIMIT)).all()
    # A practice launch's own name is pretend (maybe someone else's real site): link the practice address instead.
    site = (f"https://{plan.site_host}/" if plan and plan.mode == "full" and not b.practice
            else site_url(b.subdomain, settings) if b.subdomain else None)
    return {
        "business": {"id": b.id, "name": b.name, "site_url": site, "has_owner_email": bool(owner_emails(session, b.id)),
                     "practice": b.practice, "public": is_public(b) and not b.paused},
        "plan": {"id": plan.id, "mode": plan.mode, "site_host": plan.site_host, "mailbox": plan.mailbox}
        if plan else ({"id": latest_plan.id, "mode": latest_plan.mode, "site_host": latest_plan.site_host,
                       "mailbox": latest_plan.mailbox} if latest_plan else None),
        "practice": practice,
        "ready": ready, "headline": title, "left": left, "run": run, "proof": proven,
        "launch": launch_out(plan or latest_plan),
        "monitoring": {"enabled": settings.monitor_enabled, "every_minutes": QUICK_MINUTES,
                       "last_quick": last("monitor_quick"), "last_daily": last("monitor_daily"),
                       "cert_days_left": info.get("cert_days_left"), "domain_days_left": info.get("domain_days_left")},
        "audit": [{"at": iso(e.created_at), "actor": e.actor, "action": e.action, "target": e.target,
                   "result": e.result, "detail": e.detail} for e in events],
        "admin": admin,
        "demo_fault": b.demo_fault if admin else None,
    }

"""Renewals (S10, feature 18): what runs out, when, and who renews it. It NEVER renews or pays by itself:
money always needs a person. One set of alert thresholds for things a person renews; the certificate is
renewed by Caddy on its own (about 30 days before the end), so its first warning comes later."""

from datetime import date

from app.config import Settings

THRESHOLDS = (30, 7, 1)  # domain names and the team mailbox: a person has to renew (and pay)
CERT_THRESHOLDS = (7, 1)  # Caddy renews ~30 days ahead; a warning before 7 days left would be noise


def state(days: int | None) -> str:
    if days is None:
        return "unknown"
    if days < 0:
        return "lapsed"
    if days <= 7:
        return "urgent"
    if days <= 30:
        return "soon"
    return "ok"


def mailbox_days(settings: Settings, today: date | None = None) -> int | None:
    end = settings.mailbox_expires_on
    return None if end is None else (end - (today or date.today())).days


def item(what: str, label: str, days: int | None, who: str, plain: str) -> dict:
    return {"what": what, "label": label, "days_left": days, "state": state(days), "who": who, "plain": plain}


def card(settings: Settings, mode: str, zone: str, info: dict, today: date | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """The Renewals card on a live shop's report. `info` is the latest check run's info_json."""
    out = [item("certificate", "Security certificate (the padlock)", info.get("cert_days_left"), "automatic",
                "Renews by itself, for free. We check it every day and tell you if it doesn't.")]
    if mode == "full":
        out.append(item("domain", f"Your website name ({zone})", info.get("domain_days_left"), "you",
                        "Renewing costs money, so we never do it for you. We'll remind you 30, 7 and 1 days before."))
    else:
        out.append(item("domain", f"{settings.app_domain} (your shop's address lives under it)",
                        info.get("app_domain_days_left"), "team",
                        "Our team renews it. You don't need to do anything."))
    out.append(item("mailbox", f"Our mailbox that sends your order emails ({settings.smtp_user})",
                    mailbox_days(settings, today), "team", "Our team renews it. You don't need to do anything."))
    return out


def nearest(items: list[dict]) -> dict | None:
    """The renewal that needs attention soonest (for "My shops"), or None when all are fine/unknown."""
    due = [i for i in items if i["state"] in ("soon", "urgent", "lapsed")]
    return min(due, key=lambda i: i["days_left"]) if due else None


def crossed(days: int | None, thresholds: tuple[int, ...]) -> list[int]:
    return [] if days is None else [t for t in thresholds if days <= t]
EOF

CERT_THRESHOLDS = (7, 1)  # Caddy renews ~30 days ahead; a warning before 7 days left would be noise


def state(days: int | None) -> str:
    if days is None:
        return "unknown"
    if days < 0:
        return "lapsed"
    if days <= 7:
        return "urgent"
    if days <= 30:
        return "soon"
    return "ok"


def mailbox_days(settings: Settings, today: date | None = None) -> int | None:
    end = settings.mailbox_expires_on
    return None if end is None else (end - (today or date.today())).days


def item(what: str, label: str, days: int | None, who: str, plain: str) -> dict:
    return {"what": what, "label": label, "days_left": days, "state": state(days), "who": who, "plain": plain}


def card(settings: Settings, mode: str, zone: str, info: dict, today: date | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """The Renewals card on a live shop's report. `info` is the latest check run's info_json."""
    out = [item("certificate", "Security certificate (the padlock)", info.get("cert_days_left"), "automatic",
                "Renews by itself, for free. We check it every day and tell you if it doesn't.")]
    if mode == "full":
        out.append(item("domain", f"Your website name ({zone})", info.get("domain_days_left"), "you",
                        "Renewing costs money, so we never do it for you. We'll remind you 30, 7 and 1 days before."))
    else:
        out.append(item("domain", f"{settings.app_domain} (your shop's address lives under it)",
                        info.get("app_domain_days_left"), "team",
                        "Our team renews it. You don't need to do anything."))
    out.append(item("mailbox", f"Our mailbox that sends your order emails ({settings.smtp_user})",
                    mailbox_days(settings, today), "team", "Our team renews it. You don't need to do anything."))
    return out


def nearest(items: list[dict]) -> dict | None:
    """The renewal that needs attention soonest (for "My shops"), or None when all are fine/unknown."""
    due = [i for i in items if i["state"] in ("soon", "urgent", "lapsed")]
    return min(due, key=lambda i: i["days_left"]) if due else None


def crossed(days: int | None, thresholds: tuple[int, ...]) -> list[int]:
    return [] if days is None else [t for t in thresholds if days <= t]

"""Zone hygiene for our own shop zone (S10, feature 16, scoped down).

Once a day we compare every A record on the app's domain with the shops in the database:
- **dangling**: a record for a shop name that is deleted, not live, or practice. Anyone who later takes that
  name would inherit a working address, and a stray record points customers at a "not found" page.
- **missing**: a live shop whose address has no record: customers can't reach it.
- **wrong_target**: a shop's record points anywhere other than SERVER_IP.

Nothing is changed by the scan. Each finding carries a proposed fix; the admin approves it on the team page,
and only then is it applied through the guarded GoDaddy client (which itself refuses anything but an A record
for a shop name). Never `@`, `www`, `*`, a reserved name, MX, TXT or CNAME. Every step is audit-logged.
"""

from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit
from app.config import Settings
from app.models import Business, ZoneFinding, utcnow
from app.sites.hosts import slug_problem

TTL = 600


def shop_names(records: list[dict]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """A records whose name could be a shop (everything else in the zone is never looked at)."""
    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for r in records:
        name = str(r.get("name", "")).lower()
        if r.get("type") == "A" and name not in ("@", "www", "*") and slug_problem(name) is None:
            out.setdefault(name, []).append(str(r.get("data", "")))
    return out


def compare(settings: Settings, session: Session, records: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """What's wrong right now: [{kind, name, found, want, fix, plain, business_id}]. Reads only."""
    zone, ip = settings.app_domain, settings.server_ip
    have = shop_names(records)
    shops = {b.subdomain: b for b in session.exec(select(Business).where(Business.subdomain != None)).all()}  # noqa: E711
    out = []
    for name, datas in sorted(have.items()):
        b = shops.get(name)
        if b is None or b.practice or b.status != "live":
            why = "no shop has this name" if b is None else "this shop isn't live"
            out.append({"kind": "dangling", "name": name, "found": ", ".join(datas), "want": "", "fix": "delete",
                        "business_id": b.id if b else None,
                        "plain": f"{name}.{zone} still points at a server, but {why}. Remove the record."})
        elif sorted(datas) != [ip]:
            out.append({"kind": "wrong_target", "name": name, "found": ", ".join(datas), "want": ip, "fix": "set",
                        "business_id": b.id,
                        "plain": f"{name}.{zone} points at {', '.join(datas)}, not at our server {ip}. Point it here."})
    for name, b in sorted(shops.items()):
        if b.status == "live" and not b.practice and name not in have and slug_problem(name) is None:
            out.append({"kind": "missing", "name": name, "found": "", "want": ip, "fix": "set", "business_id": b.id,
                        "plain": f"{b.name} is live but {name}.{zone} has no address record. Add it."})
    return out


def scan(engine: Engine, settings: Settings, godaddy) -> list[ZoneFinding]:
    """Read the zone, record new findings as proposals, close the ones that went away. Returns open findings."""
    records = godaddy.get_records(settings.app_domain)
    with Session(engine) as s:
        now = compare(settings, s, records)
        keys = {(f["kind"], f["name"]) for f in now}
        open_ = s.exec(select(ZoneFinding).where(ZoneFinding.status == "open")).all()
        for f in open_:
            if (f.kind, f.name) not in keys:
                f.status, f.decided_at, f.result = "gone", utcnow(), "no longer found"
                s.add(f)
        known = {(f.kind, f.name) for f in open_}
        for f in now:
            if (f["kind"], f["name"]) not in known:
                s.add(ZoneFinding(**f))
                audit.record(s, actor="zone_hygiene", action="zone_finding", target=f"A {f['name']}",
                             result="proposed", business_id=None, detail=f["plain"][:300])
        s.commit()
        audit.record(s, actor="zone_hygiene", action="zone_scan", target=settings.app_domain, result="ok",
                     detail=f"{len(records)} records read, {len(now)} finding(s)")
        return list(s.exec(select(ZoneFinding).where(ZoneFinding.status == "open")).all())


class NoLongerTrue(Exception):
    pass


def approve(engine: Engine, settings: Settings, godaddy, finding_id: int, by: str) -> ZoneFinding:
    """The admin said yes: check the finding still holds, then apply its fix through the guarded client."""
    with Session(engine) as s:
        f = s.get(ZoneFinding, finding_id)
        if f is None or f.status != "open":
            raise LookupError("finding")
        still = {(x["kind"], x["name"]): x for x in compare(settings, s, godaddy.get_records(settings.app_domain))}
        if (f.kind, f.name) not in still:
            f.status, f.decided_at, f.decided_by, f.result = "gone", utcnow(), by, "no longer true when approved"
            s.add(f)
            s.commit()
            raise NoLongerTrue(f.name)
        before = f.found
        try:
            if f.fix == "delete":
                godaddy.delete_records(settings.app_domain, "A", f.name)
            else:
                godaddy.set_records(settings.app_domain, "A", f.name, [{"data": settings.server_ip, "ttl": TTL}])
            f.status, f.result = "fixed", "ok"
        except Exception as e:  # e.g. the guard refused, or GoDaddy failed: stays open, nothing assumed
            f.result = f"failed: {type(e).__name__}"
        f.decided_at, f.decided_by = utcnow(), by
        s.add(f)
        s.commit()
        audit.record(s, actor="admin", action="zone_fix", target=f"A {f.name}", result="ok" if f.status == "fixed" else "failed",
                     detail=f"{f.fix} {f.name}: before [{before}] after [{'' if f.fix == 'delete' else settings.server_ip}]"
                            f" approved by {by}; {f.result}"[:300])
        s.refresh(f)
        return f


def dismiss(engine: Engine, finding_id: int, by: str) -> ZoneFinding:
    with Session(engine) as s:
        f = s.get(ZoneFinding, finding_id)
        if f is None or f.status != "open":
            raise LookupError("finding")
        f.status, f.decided_at, f.decided_by, f.result = "dismissed", utcnow(), by, "left as it is"
        s.add(f)
        s.commit()
        audit.record(s, actor="admin", action="zone_dismiss", target=f"A {f.name}", result="ok", detail=f"by {by}")
        s.refresh(f)
        return f


def finding_out(f: ZoneFinding) -> dict:
    return {"id": f.id, "kind": f.kind, "name": f.name, "found": f.found, "want": f.want, "fix": f.fix,
            "plain": f.plain, "status": f.status, "result": f.result, "business_id": f.business_id,
            "created_at": f.created_at.isoformat(), "decided_by": f.decided_by}

"""Zone hygiene for our own shop zone (S10, feature 16, scoped down).

Once a day we compare every A record on the app's domain with the shops in the database:
- **dangling**: a record for a shop name that is deleted, not live, or practice. Anyone who later takes that
  name would inherit a working address, and a stray record points customers at a "not found" page.
- **missing**: a live shop whose address has no record: customers can't reach it.
- **wrong_target**: a shop's record points anywhere other than SERVER_IP.

Nothing is changed by the scan. Each finding carries a proposed fix; the admin approves it on the team page,
and only then is it applied through the guarded GoDaddy client (which itself refuses anything but an A record
for a shop name). Never `@`, `www`, `*`, a reserved name, MX, TXT or CNAME. Every step is audit-logged.
"""

from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit
from app.config import Settings
from app.models import Business, ZoneFinding, utcnow
from app.sites.hosts import slug_problem

TTL = 600


def shop_names(records: list[dict]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """A records whose name could be a shop (everything else in the zone is never looked at)."""
    out: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for r in records:
        name = str(r.get("name", "")).lower()
        if r.get("type") == "A" and name not in ("@", "www", "*") and slug_problem(name) is None:
            out.setdefault(name, []).append(str(r.get("data", "")))
    return out


def compare(settings: Settings, session: Session, records: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """What's wrong right now: [{kind, name, found, want, fix, plain, business_id}]. Reads only."""
    zone, ip = settings.app_domain, settings.server_ip
    have = shop_names(records)
    shops = {b.subdomain: b for b in session.exec(select(Business).where(Business.subdomain != None)).all()}  # noqa: E711
    out = []
    for name, datas in sorted(have.items()):
        b = shops.get(name)
        if b is None or b.practice or b.status != "live":
            why = "no shop has this name" if b is None else "this shop isn't live"
            out.append({"kind": "dangling", "name": name, "found": ", ".join(datas), "want": "", "fix": "delete",
                        "business_id": b.id if b else None,
                        "plain": f"{name}.{zone} still points at a server, but {why}. Remove the record."})
        elif sorted(datas) != [ip]:
            out.append({"kind": "wrong_target", "name": name, "found": ", ".join(datas), "want": ip, "fix": "set",
                        "business_id": b.id,
                        "plain": f"{name}.{zone} points at {', '.join(datas)}, not at our server {ip}. Point it here."})
    for name, b in sorted(shops.items()):
        if b.status == "live" and not b.practice and name not in have and slug_problem(name) is None:
            out.append({"kind": "missing", "name": name, "found": "", "want": ip, "fix": "set", "business_id": b.id,
                        "plain": f"{b.name} is live but {name}.{zone} has no address record. Add it."})
    return out


def scan(engine: Engine, settings: Settings, godaddy) -> list[ZoneFinding]:
    """Read the zone, record new findings as proposals, close the ones that went away. Returns open findings."""
    records = godaddy.get_records(settings.app_domain)
    with Session(engine) as s:
        now = compare(settings, s, records)
        keys = {(f["kind"], f["name"]) for f in now}
        open_ = s.exec(select(ZoneFinding).where(ZoneFinding.status == "open")).all()
        for f in open_:
            if (f.kind, f.name) not in keys:
                f.status, f.decided_at, f.result = "gone", utcnow(), "no longer found"
                s.add(f)
        known = {(f.kind, f.name) for f in open_}
        for f in now:
            if (f["kind"], f["name"]) not in known:
                s.add(ZoneFinding(**f))
                audit.record(s, actor="zone_hygiene", action="zone_finding", target=f"A {f['name']}",
                             result="proposed", business_id=None, detail=f["plain"][:300])
        s.commit()
        audit.record(s, actor="zone_hygiene", action="zone_scan", target=settings.app_domain, result="ok",
                     detail=f"{len(records)} records read, {len(now)} finding(s)")
        return list(s.exec(select(ZoneFinding).where(ZoneFinding.status == "open")).all())


class NoLongerTrue(Exception):
    pass


def approve(engine: Engine, settings: Settings, godaddy, finding_id: int, by: str) -> ZoneFinding:
    """The admin said yes: check the finding still holds, then apply its fix through the guarded client."""
    with Session(engine) as s:
        f = s.get(ZoneFinding, finding_id)
        if f is None or f.status != "open":
            raise LookupError("finding")
        still = {(x["kind"], x["name"]): x for x in compare(settings, s, godaddy.get_records(settings.app_domain))}
        if (f.kind, f.name) not in still:
            f.status, f.decided_at, f.decided_by, f.result = "gone", utcnow(), by, "no longer true when approved"
            s.add(f)
            s.commit()
            raise NoLongerTrue(f.name)
        before = f.found
        try:
            if f.fix == "delete":
                godaddy.delete_records(settings.app_domain, "A", f.name)
            else:
                godaddy.set_records(settings.app_domain, "A", f.name, [{"data": settings.server_ip, "ttl": TTL}])
            f.status, f.result = "fixed", "ok"
        except Exception as e:  # e.g. the guard refused, or GoDaddy failed: stays open, nothing assumed
            f.result = f"failed: {type(e).__name__}"
        f.decided_at, f.decided_by = utcnow(), by
        s.add(f)
        s.commit()
        audit.record(s, actor="admin", action="zone_fix", target=f"A {f.name}", result="ok" if f.status == "fixed" else "failed",
                     detail=f"{f.fix} {f.name}: before [{before}] after [{'' if f.fix == 'delete' else settings.server_ip}]"
                            f" approved by {by}; {f.result}"[:300])
        s.refresh(f)
        return f


def dismiss(engine: Engine, finding_id: int, by: str) -> ZoneFinding:
    with Session(engine) as s:
        f = s.get(ZoneFinding, finding_id)
        if f is None or f.status != "open":
            raise LookupError("finding")
        f.status, f.decided_at, f.decided_by, f.result = "dismissed", utcnow(), by, "left as it is"
        s.add(f)
        s.commit()
        audit.record(s, actor="admin", action="zone_dismiss", target=f"A {f.name}", result="ok", detail=f"by {by}")
        s.refresh(f)
        return f


def finding_out(f: ZoneFinding) -> dict:
    return {"id": f.id, "kind": f.kind, "name": f.name, "found": f.found, "want": f.want, "fix": f.fix,
            "plain": f.plain, "status": f.status, "result": f.result, "business_id": f.business_id,
            "created_at": f.created_at.isoformat(), "decided_by": f.decided_by}
